interaction.content: Hello, Xiaotian. Lately I’ve been feeling really awful and don’t know what to do, so I came to talk with you.
Hello, welcome. How would you like me to address you?
You can call me Xiao Zhu.
Okay, Xiao Zhu. In our sessions, everything we talk about will be kept confidential, and we’ll strictly follow ethical guidelines. If you don’t have other questions, we can start our first session.
Okay, let’s start.
We have about 50 minutes to talk about the things in your life that you care about.
I’m four months pregnant now, and my physical condition isn’t very good. The morning sickness is really bad, and I feel weak every day.
Mm-hmm, go on, I’m listening.

Recently I feel more and more defeated. I can’t get interested in anything. Almost every day is just eating, throwing up, and passing out asleep. Even taking a shower or going out takes a lot of courage and motivation.
Mm-hmm.
Before, I had just started my career, but because the pregnancy symptoms are so severe, now I can only rest at home and my work has stopped.
Oh, the pregnancy symptoms are really severe. This period is indeed not easy.
Yeah, I feel very helpless every day.
It sounds like your current situation makes you feel really helpless, especially with your career just getting started.
What’s worse is that my husband is often away from home because of work, so I’m the only one at home. It’s really lonely.
I can understand that you feel lonely because your husband isn’t home often. This period must be really hard to get through for you.
Yeah, I really wish someone could be with me so I wouldn’t feel so alone.
That wish is very natural. In this kind of situation, we all long for someone to accompany and support us, especially when you’re facing so many challenges.
Right. Before I got pregnant, I could basically handle my emotions and anxiety pretty well, and I never had a breakdown.
It sounds like a tough experience. Would you be willing to talk about what happened then?
After I got pregnant, the changes in my body caught me off guard, and on top of that, no one around me seems to understand how I feel, so the pressure just keeps building.
Mm, I hear the pressure you’re under and how you’re feeling. It’s really not easy.
Yes, especially every time I talk to friends or family, they all say, “Every pregnant woman goes through this,” which makes me feel really helpless.
It sounds really helpless. The feelings you’re describing are very real.
At first my willpower was still pretty strong, and I kept telling myself to be tough. But lately it’s getting harder and harder to hold on.
I can understand that the recent pressure is making it harder for you to keep going.
Yes, before I could still support myself by planning for the future, but now there’s nothing that can really motivate me.
I’d like to understand more. When you think about this, how do you feel inside?
I feel really low, like I’m stuck in a helpless state.
It sounds like your mood is very low right now. How long has this feeling been going on?
About a month and a half. I increasingly feel like I’ve lost a lot of control in this process.
It sounds like you feel you’ve lost a lot of your sense of control, is that right?
Yeah, the drastic weight changes also make me feel really bad.
The changes in your weight also seem to be troubling you a lot.
Yes, I keep worrying that my physical condition will affect the baby.
That’s understandable. When you’re trying to conceive and pregnant, you do pay special attention to your physical condition.
Yes, sometimes I can’t help wanting to eat more, hoping to ease my emotions through food.
I see. Besides eating, do you have any other ways to relieve stress and deal with difficult emotions?
Sometimes I’ll watch TV dramas or listen to some music, but those only help for a little while.
How do you feel about this?
I feel like these methods can’t really solve the problem. They’re more like a temporary escape.
It sounds like these activities are just temporary comfort for you, and you feel they don’t solve the root problem.
Yes, sometimes I feel like I’m stuck in a dilemma and can’t get out.
When you feel stuck like this, have you talked to anyone about it?
Sometimes I talk to my husband, but he’s very busy with work and is often not at home.
Mm-hmm, it sounds like you need someone who can really listen to you. You’re hoping to find an outlet through this conversation, to let out these negative emotions, is that right?
Yes, I hope I can find an outlet so these negative emotions have somewhere to go.
I’m very willing to listen to you.
Thank you, Xiaotian.

We just talked a bit about your expectations for life. You mentioned you’ve been trying to conceive recently, but the process hasn’t been smooth, with the pandemic, your physical condition, and so on affecting things.
Yes, it feels like nothing is under my control.
You hope there’s someone who can talk with you about your unhappiness. Besides that, do you have any other expectations?
I hope I can find some effective ways to ease my emotions, instead of going on like this in a slump.
I notice you have a strong desire to get out of this difficult situation, and that takes a lot of courage.
Thank you. I also really want to get back to a normal life as soon as possible.
You also mentioned that people around you aren’t willing to listen to you. I’m curious, how do you sense when someone is “willing” or “unwilling” to listen?
Because every time I talk about it, their responses are very perfunctory. It feels like they don’t really care about how I feel.
It sounds like their reactions make you feel uncared for and not accepted.
Yes, I feel misunderstood and uncared for.
Yeah, it’s like all those “negative” emotions don’t have anywhere to go.
Right, so these negative emotions just keep piling up and affecting my life more and more.
That does sound really painful. Have you done anything like this before?
Actually, I tried keeping a journal, but I could never stick with it.

I understand. Keeping a journal really does take some persistence, and not everyone can keep it up. Maybe later we can talk about some other methods and see if there are any small activities that work for you.
I can give it a try. I hope it helps.
I hear you saying you don’t really want people around you to know you have these negative emotions.
Yes, I don’t really want people around me to know I have so many negative emotions.

I can understand how you feel. Not wanting others to know might be because you care a lot about what they think. Maybe you could share a bit more about your worries, and then we can discuss a small method that suits you. How does that sound?
Okay. I’m worried that if they find out, they’ll think I’m a burden and won’t want to bother with me anymore.
Who are you most worried might discover this secret?
Mainly my husband and my friends.
That makes sense. Are you worried about how they might react if they find out?
I know they all have their own things to deal with, and I don’t want to make them worry about me too.
I hear that you can tell which things you want to keep in your own heart. Could you talk a bit more about how you think about this?
Yeah, I always feel like I shouldn’t pass my negative emotions on to other people.
I understand how you feel. Maybe we can talk more about the difficulty you’re sensing there, okay?
Every time I want to open my mouth and say something, it feels really hard to start. I’m afraid of being misunderstood or disliked.
Mm, I get it. It seems like there’s a big gap between wanting to express yourself and actually doing it.
Yes, I always feel like my feelings aren’t important and that others won’t understand.
Sometimes, certain past experiences leave marks inside us.
Yes, it feels like some emotions were never really dealt with and have just been piling up in my heart.
The hurts from childhood can turn into scars, and sometimes they can start to ache again.
Yes, that feeling has always been there.
I can understand; that feeling really is very painful.
Yeah, sometimes I feel like I’m about to reach my limit.
What kind of change do you hope to see in yourself?
I hope I can be strong, be able to handle these emotions, and not let them affect my life.
In terms of relationships, what kind of changes do you hope for?
I hope I can express my feelings more confidently and not be so afraid of how others will react.
In the future, when we have the chance, we can move toward that wish together and see how it goes.
Okay, thank you.
We’ll take it slowly, and we’ll work on it together.
Thank you, Xiaotian. I’ll do my best.

Mm-hmm. I think the worries in our hearts usually can’t be solved in just one conversation. If you’re willing, we can schedule another time and continue talking about the issues you care about. Would you be open to that?
Okay, I’m willing.
Okay.
Thank you, I really appreciate it.

Up to this point, I’d like to give a brief summary of what we’ve talked about. You mentioned some pressures and challenges in your life, like trying to conceive, travel plans, changes in your body, and relationships. Is there anything in particular you were hoping to talk about in this session that we haven’t covered?
I think you already have a general understanding of my situation. Right now I mainly hope to find some ways to ease my emotions.

Okay~ I see that Xiao Zhu hopes to be someone with stable emotions and the ability to handle things. In your current life, finding ways to relieve your stress is something we can work on at this stage.
Yes, I also hope to find some positive ways to face these problems.

I’d like to invite you to try two small exercises, and you can see what you think. The first is to say one encouraging sentence to yourself every night before you go to sleep. You can say it out loud, or write it in the notes on your phone.
Mm, I can try that.

It would be good if the encouraging words are a bit specific, like acknowledging some of your abilities or qualities, or expressing acceptance and confidence toward yourself. You can be creative with it~
Got it, I’ll take it seriously.

The second exercise is to jot down what happens when you feel low between today and our session next week: what happened, what you were thinking, and what you did. You can just write it in your phone’s notes or on little slips of paper, like a mini diary. Writing these things down may help with your emotions, and next time we can talk about your notes. How does that sound?
Okay, I think that sounds like a good idea. I’ll try to keep a record.

It really takes courage to face yourself. Let’s work on this together~ If we follow the usual setup for counseling, would meeting at this time next week work for you? Or if you prefer another time, you can also suggest it.
Next week at this time is fine, but I’m also free the afternoon of the day after tomorrow.
Got it, is that 2 p.m. the day after tomorrow?
Yes, 2 p.m.
Would Friday at 2 p.m. work? My work schedule is already set, I’m sorry.
It’s okay, 2 p.m. is fine.
Okay, then you can make the appointment directly in the mini program.
Okay, I’ll book it.
Alright, when the time comes the mini program will send a reminder. So we’ll set it for August 5th (Friday) at 2 p.m.
Okay, thank you.
Sorry, I wrote the wrong date. Would 10 a.m. work for you? I also have something scheduled at 4 p.m.
10 a.m. is fine too.

Okay. Or you can also just log in at 2 p.m. if you prefer; it depends on what time you’d like. Let’s just set it now. At the end I’ll send you two questionnaires about the effectiveness of the counseling, so we can better understand your experience and support you better in the future. Please let me know after you’ve filled them out, thank you.
Good morning, teacher.
Good morning. You mentioned feeling very anxious. Could you tell me more specifically what’s going on?

When I’m memorizing, I always feel like I’m doing it wrong, and I get really anxious. I keep doubting whether what I’m memorizing now is actually important, whether it’ll be on the exam. It feels like even if I memorize it, it’s useless. Either I want to memorize everything, or I feel like this stuff isn’t important.
This kind of doubt and anxiety really bothers you. Can you say more about how exactly it affects you?
Yeah, my progress is always behind what I expect. I’ve tried to adjust my schedule, but it hasn’t worked well. Every time I end up giving up halfway and stop memorizing.
I get what you’re struggling with. It seems like your pace of progress is also something you care a lot about. Have you tried any specific ways to adjust your pace?

Actually, I’ve also been paying attention to other people’s progress, and I’ve heard some classmates share their study methods. But every time I see them moving along smoothly, I get even more anxious and discouraged, and feel like I’m much worse than they are.
Seeing other people’s progress and methods makes you feel even more anxious and self-blaming. In what specific ways does that feeling affect you?

This anxiety makes it impossible for me to focus on memorizing. My mind keeps wandering to other things. Sometimes I even feel like I’m just not as good as others, and there’s this voice inside saying, “Forget it, just leave it,” and then I stop studying.
Mm, I see. This self-doubt and anxiety are blocking your motivation to study. It really feels very hard for you.
Got it, no worries.
I just reconnected the internet. Can you receive my messages now?
Yes, I can see them now, teacher.
Did something happen yesterday that made your anxiety worse?

Last night one of my roommates in the dorm shared with me how much she’d studied. After I heard that, I felt really anxious, afraid they’d do better than me. I know it’s not right to think like that, but I just can’t control it.
I understand, that kind of anxiety is really hard to ignore. So does this anxiety show up when you’re studying and affect your pace?
Yes, teacher. Once I start feeling anxious, it’s really hard to concentrate, so my progress becomes very slow, and sometimes I just give up.
I see, this feeling brings you a lot of pressure. About when did this fear start?
This fear has actually been around for a while, probably since my sophomore year. I’m always afraid I’m not studying well enough, afraid others will surpass me.
It sounds like this pressure has been going on for some time and is affecting your studying and your mood. Could you tell me in more detail what specific situations usually trigger this anxiety?
Yeah, I require myself to at least finish memorizing one chapter a day, but I always feel like I can’t get it done, and inside I feel this pressure of not being able to complete the task.
Mm-hmm. What do you think is having the key impact on your progress?
I feel like there’s something wrong with my way of memorizing.
Your way of memorizing?
Yes, maybe the method isn’t efficient enough. I keep feeling like I need to improve it, but I don’t know how much improvement would actually be better.
From when you started preparing for the exam until now, have you made any changes to your memorizing methods?
I’ve tried some new methods, like using image scanning instead of typing everything out by hand. That saves a bit of time, but the effect still isn’t obvious.
Mm, it sounds like you’ve been constantly looking for more efficient ways to memorize. How did you come up with using image scanning?
I learned it from some top students’ exam-prep videos on Bilibili.
So you’ve been watching some study-method videos on Bilibili?
Yes, I often go on Bilibili to watch videos about study methods, hoping to find ways to improve my efficiency.
Were there other methods on there, and you chose this one instead of the others?
There were lots of methods. I tried a few and found that the image-scanning one suited me better, so I stuck with it.
I see. What kind of methods do you find relatively effective for you?
Mm, sometimes I also feel that besides hard work, there are things like luck or other factors that influence the outcome.
Does thinking that way help you at all?
It does help. Thinking about those things makes me feel a bit lighter, like I’m not putting all the responsibility only on myself.

Right, sometimes taking non-personal factors into account can indeed reduce our pressure. You just mentioned that the image-scanning method works for you. Can you say more specifically how it helps you?
Yes, teacher. In high school my grades were always pretty good.
That’s great. Can you share a bit about how you improved your study efficiency and kept your grades up back then?
Yeah, my study methods were more regular back then, and I was confident, so my grades stayed very stable.
You mentioned confidence, calmness, putting in time, and the teacher’s arrangements.
Yes, all of those were important. Back then my confidence was strong, my emotions were relatively stable, and the study schedule arranged by the teachers was very organized.
Mm, it sounds like those factors really played a big role in how you did.
Yeah, I really performed well at that time.
Are those factors still there now?
Some of them are, like I’m still willing to put in the time, but the confidence and emotional stability parts have dropped a lot.
I understand. You mentioned changes in your confidence and emotions. Can you tell me more specifically what those changes are like?
Mm, now I can feel my anxiety and pressure more clearly, and even if I let them out, it doesn’t necessarily solve the problem.
It seems this anxiety and pressure have a big impact on you. Back then, did you also feel similar emotions?
Yes, but back then I might have been better at controlling my emotions. They wouldn’t affect me as much as the anxiety does now.
From what you’re saying, even when you didn’t review much and were playing games, things were still okay. Could you share with me what your study situation was like at that time?
Back then my foundation was probably solid, and the pressure of the college entrance exam actually pushed my study efficiency up.
I see. When you were at home playing games back then, did you ever occasionally think about your classmates’ progress?
A little, but it wasn’t as intense as it is now. At that time I was still fairly confident in myself and not too worried about being overtaken by others.
Got it. That confidence back then seems to have helped you overcome some of the anxiety.
Yes, teacher. As I’ve gotten older and the material has gotten harder, it feels like my confidence isn’t what it used to be.
Over these years, what kinds of things have made you feel your confidence has decreased?
Probably some failed exams. Little by little I started doubting my own ability, and the fear of failing has gotten stronger and stronger.
I see. Facing those failures, you probably have a lot of mixed feelings inside, right?
Yes. If I don’t really learn it and just rush the progress, I feel like I’m wasting time, and I feel really conflicted inside.
I can hear that you care a lot about how you use your time and about the effectiveness of your studying. That can be quite a challenge for you.
I feel like it’s just staying on the surface, not really understanding the knowledge points, just rushing to finish tasks.
What is “staying on the surface” like for you?
It’s like clearly knowing I haven’t fully grasped some knowledge points, but in order to keep up with the schedule I just gloss over them, and I still don’t feel at ease inside.
How do you tell the difference between staying on the surface and really understanding?
I think if I can use the knowledge points flexibly, and the questions don’t feel unfamiliar when I do them, and I can understand the essence of the problems, then that counts as truly understanding.
I see. A lot of people feel very troubled when they run into difficulties with questions, and they’ll go back and review the knowledge points. How does that feel for you?
For me, that process is necessary, but it makes me feel like there isn’t enough time. Inside I’m always chasing the schedule, and I feel very anxious.
You just mentioned feeling like there isn’t enough time and that you’re chasing the schedule. In that situation, how do you usually cope?

That process makes me feel like time isn’t enough, and once I can’t solve a problem, there’s this inner voice that questions, “You haven’t even learned the knowledge properly, why are you in such a hurry to do questions?” and then I get even more anxious.
At that moment, a voice like “You haven’t even learned the knowledge properly, why are you in such a hurry to do questions?” shows up inside, right?
Yes, teacher. That kind of voice comes up a lot and questions the meaning of what I’m doing right now.
Mm-hmm. And if you get a question wrong, then what happens?
If I get a question wrong, I feel really frustrated and think I have no ability at all to master this knowledge.
Has anyone ever said to you or people around you things like “You don’t know this, you don’t know that,” or criticized you in a similar tone?
Yes, especially teachers and my parents. When I didn’t do well, they used that kind of wording to criticize me, and now it feels like those words have become the voice inside me.
You’d rather fail the course than go take the exam. Is it because you’re afraid of facing possible failure?
Yeah, sometimes I feel like if I expect the exam to go terribly, I’d rather avoid it and not face the failure.
I can understand how you feel. That kind of thinking can feel really painful, but we can explore together how to face these challenges.
Yeah, teacher, this way of thinking makes me feel bad about myself too, but sometimes I really can’t face a disappointing result.
Sometimes this can become an inner voice that comes out to criticize you.
Yes, it feels like those voices have already become part of my subconscious and often hit me when I’m trying hard.
Accepting yourself is a long, repetitive process. Even now I find I’ve forgotten a lot of things. The parts of myself I didn’t want to accept have all sunk to the bottom of my memory.
It does sound like that. I also often try to avoid the parts I don’t want to accept, but it seems the more I do that, the more strongly those parts affect me.

Recently I’ve been in supervision, taking a course with a teacher from Taiwan, and a lot of memories have started to surface again. I realized I had forgotten them. I stubbornly tried to only be the version of myself I liked, but the imperfect self is also a part of me.
Mm, hearing you say that, I also feel like it’s time for me to face those neglected parts. The imperfect self also needs to be accepted.

Yes, the process of accepting yourself takes time and patience. Facing and acknowledging those parts actually helps us understand ourselves more fully. Have you tried any ways to help you better accept those imperfect parts?
Teacher, I really haven’t paid much attention to that yet. I’m not sure whether this kind of information will be helpful for my future development.
You can think about your current state and needs, and then gradually explore some strategies and methods that suit you. That will be helpful for your future development and personal growth.
Oh, I see. I still need to learn more about these things; they might be helpful for my future.
Yes, getting to know yourself and finding methods that fit you is an important process. If you have any questions or needs, we can explore them together and find solutions that work for you.
Mm-hmm, teacher, I probably still need to explore and discover more.

Maybe it’s something that needs to be discovered slowly and picked up bit by bit. Sometimes we don’t get the chance to discover it. Especially in periods that are seen as failures or not worth mentioning, there might be hidden treasures.
Yeah, I also feel like there might be a lot worth digging into in those periods, it just takes time to slowly discover them.
Those experiences that don’t look like much on the surface might actually have a lot worth paying attention to.
It really is a bit like what that book said, that many things require us to calm down and slowly find the answers.
Yes, sometimes the answers don’t show up right away. We need time and experiences to really feel them.
Yes, the experiences themselves might be a process of discovery, getting to know ourselves through them.
These experiences not only help us grow, they also help us understand ourselves better.
Dreaming? What kind of experience is that like, teacher?
Yes, sometimes through dreams or stories we can also get some insight and understanding about our inner world.
I see. Your experience sounds really interesting, teacher. It seems like every stage of life might hide unexpected gains.
So, congratulations on discovering the parts of yourself you haven’t accepted yet.
Thank you, teacher. I’ll try to accept myself and explore those parts that haven’t been accepted.

In narrative therapy, there’s an idea that in our lives there are always both successful and unsuccessful moments. We can try to find some positive elements in the moments that feel less successful, and in the moments that feel very successful, look for parts we might have overlooked.
That really makes a lot of sense. I’ll try to look back at myself in different periods and search for those stories that were ignored.
Right, actually everyone’s life is made up of multiple storylines. When you feel successful in your studies, maybe some other areas get overlooked, like love or fun. Life really is rich.
Yes, teacher, I’ve noticed that I do put a lot of effort into my studies, but I’ve neglected a lot in other areas.
Exactly, it’s hard for us to be perfect in every area. Everyone has their own priorities, and that’s normal.
True, haha, everyone has their own priorities, and it’s hard to cover everything.
Yes, everyone has areas they focus on more. There’s no right or wrong in that. What matters is that we’re aware of it and make some balance.
Yeah, sometimes when I see some classmates doing really well in other areas, I also feel a bit envious.
Sometimes we only see the successful side of others, but not the effort and difficulties behind it.
Haha, so there are little secrets too. Looks like everyone has their own story.
Yes, everyone has their own experiences and challenges, which aren’t always visible on the surface.
Got it, teacher. It seems like everyone has a complicated side that others don’t know about.
That’s right. People are often facing unspeakable challenges and issues of self-acceptance deep inside.
Yes, I also feel that in many areas I still need more acceptance and recognition of myself.
Could you share more about your thoughts and feelings in those areas?
In the future I hope I can accept myself better and also find a balance, so I’m no longer trapped by anxiety and self-doubt.
That’s a really good goal. We can explore together how to work toward it.
Yes, I’ve heard that this field might be more developed abroad.
Mm-hmm, in some places it is.
So maybe I could consider making some adjustments in my future studies, to combine them with my interests and needs?
That’s a very good idea. Do you have any specific options or target directions in mind?
Sounds pretty good. I am indeed interested, and I can learn more about this area in the future.
Yes, it’s important to understand the different options. For example, you could look at some programs abroad and also check out opportunities for development here in China.
Got it. I’ll seriously consider these options and see which one suits me better.
Mm-hmm, this kind of exploration will be very helpful for your future development.
Thank you for your suggestions, teacher. They’ve been really helpful for me.
You’re welcome. I wish you all the best. Our time for today is almost up.
Okay, teacher, time really flew by.
Shall we stop here for today, is that okay?
Yes, teacher, that’s fine. Thank you for your guidance and help today.
I’m really glad I could help you.
Haha, it feels a bit like time travel.
Yes, sometimes we do feel like time passes very quickly.
Yes, I’ll look more into the directions of different schools and hope to find something that suits me.
Okay, that kind of exploration is very meaningful. Keep it up.
Okay, see you next time, teacher.
See you next time. I wish you peace and everything going smoothly. Goodbye.
Hello, counselor.
Hello, I’m glad you’re here. Did you see the message I sent you before?
Yes, I saw it.
Okay. Is there anything in particular you want to talk about today? Do you want to continue with the topic of conflicts from last time, or is there something else?
I think I’d like to continue with the topic of conflicts from last time. There are a few things I want to talk to you about.
Okay, then let’s start with your homework from last time. Can you share what you did for it?

Last time the homework was to try to recall the times when things were pleasant between me and my parents. I thought about it, and there really were a few times when they did care about me quite a bit.
Sounds like it was a meaningful reflection. Could you tell me more about some moments that really stood out to you?
Once, when I was little, we had a dog at home. It got sick and I was really upset. My parents saw how I was and took the dog to see a vet. That made me feel like they did love me.
That sounds like a moment when they were really caring and supportive. Can you share how you felt then or afterwards?

Maybe it’s that sometimes, when I really need it, they will step in and help me. It’s just that a lot of the time their way of doing things is pretty forceful, and it’s not the kind of care I hope for, so it’s hard for me to accept.
Mm, I see. You feel that their way of doing things makes you uncomfortable, right?
I’m not very satisfied with it, but at least in those moments they try to help me. I feel like that’s their way of caring, even though sometimes what I feel more is pressure and not being understood.
I get it. That pressure and sense of not being understood is really troubling for you, isn’t it?
Yeah, but those kinds of moments are really rare. Most of the time I still feel like our communication is always full of pressure and a lack of understanding.
Could you share one or two things that left a deep impression on you?

Once I worked really hard to prepare for an exam, but I didn’t do well. When my parents saw the score, they were really angry and scolded me for not trying my best, saying I had let them down. I was really sad then and felt that no matter how hard I tried, I couldn’t get their approval.
It sounds like you were really sad at that time and felt your efforts weren’t recognized, right?

And another time, I remember some relatives came to borrow money. My parents didn’t really discuss it much and just lent it out, and afterwards life at home was really hard. I tried to talk with them about that decision, but they didn’t listen to my opinion at all. I felt like I didn’t have any say in this family.
I see. That made you feel like your opinions in the family weren’t valued, is that right?
Yeah. I think maybe deep down they do care about me, but this way of doing things makes me feel awful. What they care more about is saving face and their traditional ideas.
Did you talk to your mom about this incident too?
No. I feel like there’s no point bringing these things up with them. They’ll just think I’m picking a fight and won’t really understand how I feel.
Mm-hm. It’s like only sharing good news and not bad news has become a way of showing care for your family.
Yeah, I always feel like if I tell them about my difficulties, it’ll just make them look down on me more, and I’ll get more criticism from them.
Mm-hm, and if you tell them, it seems like they really can’t solve it right away and will just worry. But sharing your feelings can also help you feel more supported and stronger, don’t you think?
Maybe it’s like that, but right now it’s really hard for me to do. Talking to them feels more like adding to my own burden.
You feel that doing that would make you feel pressured, and you might feel uncomfortable because of how they react?
Yeah. Every time I talk to them about these things, I feel like I’m admitting that I’m incompetent. I don’t want them to think I’m not a successful person.
I can understand that. You feel that talking to them about these things makes it seem like you’re admitting a kind of powerlessness.
Yes. I don’t want them to think I can’t handle my own stuff. I want to be an adult who can face problems independently.
It seems I can really feel how often you’ve mentioned wanting to be a “grown-up.” Could you talk more specifically about what being a “grown-up” means to you?
I think being a “grown-up” means being able to handle all kinds of problems in life, being emotionally stable, not needing to rely on others, especially not needing my parents’ approval and support.
I see. You feel that facing problems independently is very important.
I don’t know. Actually, a lot of the time I feel like they won’t really acknowledge me just because I’ve grown up.
You feel that even if you become more successful, as long as your views are different from theirs, they still won’t truly recognize you, is that right?
They always insist on their own views. I feel like even if I become more successful, as long as my views are different from theirs, they still won’t really recognize me.
I hear a kind of conflict inside you. On one hand you want to do well for yourself, and on the other hand you feel tied down by your parents’ demands and judgments.
Yes, I often feel this kind of inner tearing. On one hand I want to do well for myself, and on the other hand I feel like I’m bound by my parents’ demands and evaluations.
These two feelings seem to exist in you at the same time, making you feel like you can’t fully be yourself freely, is that right?
Yeah. I don’t want them to feel hurt or unhappy because of my choices, but sometimes I feel like I’m suppressing myself.
Mm-hm.
I really hope I can find a balance, not be constrained by my parents, and still get along with them peacefully.
Mm, it sounds like you’re working hard to find a balance, and that’s really important to you.
Yeah, I feel like sometimes I’m moving too slowly, far from the state I expect of myself.
Mm. Can you tell me why you feel that way?
It probably started in high school. I saw people around me all having clear goals and directions, while I felt like I was still stuck in place, and I felt really anxious.
That period must have been very confusing for you. How do you think that experience has affected your mindset now?
Yeah. I feel like I have to accomplish something. I don’t want to be looked down on by my parents forever like I’m a child.
Mm, you hope your parents can see your growth and independence. That’s really important to you, isn’t it?
Yes. I hope they can see my efforts and growth and recognize that I’m an adult who can stand on my own.
Mm-hm, our time is up for today. It feels like you shared more of your feelings and thoughts this time, and our exploration seems to have brought some insights.
Yeah, I do feel a bit better after saying it out loud. Thank you for your time.

I feel like I can understand why you’re so eager to have the ability to handle all kinds of interpersonal conflicts, and also why you’re so afraid and tense about conflict. It all seems related to the urgency you shared today about wanting to leave your parents’ protection quickly and grow independently. I’m not sure if I’m understanding that correctly.
Yes, you understood it very accurately. This has been my confusion for a long time, and I hope I can find some direction through counseling.

Morty, good morning! I’ve been under a lot of emotional pressure lately and I’d like to talk with you about it. Especially about the differences between various forms of online counseling, I want to hear your thoughts.

I’m thinking about choosing a suitable form of online counseling, but I’m a bit confused right now and don’t really know which one is better. On the one hand, I want to save some money, on the other hand I’m worried about how effective it will be. I feel that in‑person counseling might help me feel the counselor’s support and understanding more. But sometimes it’s just not affordable. You mentioned that text might limit how your emotions come across. I’m curious, is it mainly because it lacks the nuances that come with someone’s voice?

Mainly because there’s no voice, yeah, and also it feels like there’s less sense of interaction. I feel that when there’s voice communication, especially for expressing emotions, there’s more resonance. Text can sometimes feel kind of cold, with a sense of distance.
I get it. Communication with voice can better convey subtle emotional details, and you feel that this way it’s easier for you to build a sense of closeness, right?
Yes. The intensity of emotions, the changes in tone, are really hard to fully convey through text. That’s what makes me so torn, I don’t know if choosing text is the right thing.
Your concern makes sense; text really can have trouble carrying those details. If audio or video counseling were more manageable financially for you, do you feel those might be better options?
Exactly, that’s what makes me doubt how effective text counseling is. Even though it’s cheaper, it might have big limitations.

Yeah, I feel that too, like there’s a layer of human warmth and the realness of being face‑to‑face that’s missing.
Mm, that kind of worry is very natural. Could you share with me if you’ve had any particular in‑person counseling experiences that made you feel it worked better?
There were a few times when my emotions were really up and down, and the counselor could give me comfort and support right away. I feel like that might not come through in text or audio.
That’s a very precious experience. When your emotions were intense in in‑person counseling, getting that immediate comfort and support had a big impact on you, didn’t it?
Yes, at that time I really needed that face‑to‑face support and comfort. So when I think back on it now, in‑person really does feel different.
That experience is clearly very important to you. Up to now, would you say your preference for in‑person counseling is still very strong?
Yes, I still feel that in‑person counseling works best, especially for emotional support and interaction.
That’s interesting; it seems in‑person interaction really has a lot of positive effects for you. Could you share whether your thoughts and feelings about this experience have changed at all now?
I do think about these questions more often, because I’m under more pressure now, and I also have to consider money, so I’m really torn between online and in‑person counseling.
I see. So it’s the pressure you’re facing and the financial issues that are making you hesitate about which format to choose, right?

When I’m especially free, I have more time to think about these things, especially at night when it’s quiet. When I’m especially busy, the pressure is huge and my emotions fluctuate easily, and I want even more to find someone to talk to.
It sounds like when you’re idle or under a lot of stress, you’re especially likely to get caught up in thinking and emotional swings, and you need someone to talk to even more.
I used to think online counseling might not be as effective as in‑person, but now I feel they each have their strengths, which makes me feel pretty conflicted.
I can see you’re really weighing the pros and cons of the two formats.

Sometimes I feel that working hard at studying and chasing honors is meaningless. It feels like no matter how hard I try, the emotional pressure is still there, especially in some family and social relationships where I can’t fully express my feelings and true thoughts.

You’re saying that even by studying hard and striving for honors, you still can’t really ease the emotional pressure, especially because in family and social relationships you can’t let out your real emotions, right?
Yes. My family might still judge me based on traditional ideas. Even if I have lots of honors, emotionally I’m still very confused and under a lot of pressure.
So in your family’s eyes, your honors and efforts might not be as important as their traditional standards, and that leaves you confused and stressed, is that right?

It’s not just about honors. It’s more that the pressure comes from the conflict between their expectations of me and my own real feelings. Their expectations always make me feel like I’ve lost myself.
When you say “they,” who are you including?
Yeah, especially some peers, people my age. Their views are also pretty traditional, and that’s affected how I see my own identity.
Mm, what exactly do you mean by those traditional views?
You can feel it in everyday chats and interactions. Their views on a lot of things are still stuck in some traditional frameworks, like filial duty and ethics, and that puts a lot of pressure on me.
Can you talk about how you feel that pressure in those areas?
Mm, they really stress filial duty in lots of things, like how to treat your parents, how to follow traditional customs. All of that makes me feel suffocated.
I see. What kind of trouble do their demands bring you, specifically?
Yeah, they bring it up from time to time, which makes me feel like I’m not really free.
At what moments is that feeling of not being free especially strong? Can you describe it more specifically?
My dad is relatively open‑minded, but when it comes to filial duty he’s still very strict. He often emphasizes these things together with my siblings, which puts a lot of pressure on me.
Could you say more specifically? How are they influenced by your parents? How does filial duty show up in them that makes you feel they’re not like people born in the 90s?

I feel they really listen to what the older generation teaches, especially about being filial to parents, and the demands are very strict. These ideas deeply shape their behavior and attitudes. They don’t feel like people born in the 90s, more like they’re bound by the older generation’s traditional views.
It really sounds like this is very stressful for you.
It’s my uncle.
Mm, I see.
My uncle is also someone who really stresses those traditional ideas and loves to bring them up at family gatherings.
He also seems to really emphasize filial ethics.
Yeah, it really feels like everything you do is for the sake of following those traditions, and that makes me feel very stifled.
I can sense how suffocating this is for you.
Yeah, it’s really hard to imagine that in modern society these traditional ideas still have such a strong influence on the younger people in the family.
What does he say?
He often says we must respect our elders and can’t go against their wishes. Even when choosing our own life and partner, we have to consider the elders’ opinions.
It sounds like you’re facing a lot of pressure.
Yeah, it really makes you feel suffocated, like you can’t live according to your own wishes.
What did you do at the time?
That day I really couldn’t take it anymore, so I talked to him about how I felt, hoping he’d understand my confusion, but in the end he still didn’t get it.
What impact did that outcome have on you?
It made me feel even more disappointed and helpless, like there’s no one in the family who can truly understand and support me.
Do you wish your closest peers had a different attitude?
Of course. Especially for our generation, we should be more open and understanding with each other, instead of blindly following those outdated ideas.
Mm‑hmm. How do you feel coming out to your siblings is different from coming out to other people?
Siblings are supposed to be the closest people. Their understanding and support are really important to me. If even they can’t understand, it feels even lonelier in this family.
So your siblings’ acceptance is especially important to you, right?
Yeah. Talking with friends is relatively free and open, but with my siblings I always feel this layer of pressure from traditional ideas, and I can’t fully let go.
I can understand. You feel more relaxed with friends.
Yes, it’s more relaxed with friends. They understand me and support me, which makes me feel safer.
So you feel that things are tougher on the family side, especially with people of your own generation?
Yes, the peers in the family are really the first hurdle. I didn’t expect to run into such big obstacles, and that leaves me very confused and disappointed.
I see, this really isn’t easy for you. Can you tell me more about the difficulties you’ve been facing?
Yeah, it’s like two completely different worlds. My friends’ world is free and open, while the family world is bound by traditional ideas.
That makes sense. Can you talk in more detail about what goes through your mind in these different environments?

People born after ’95 are generally more open, willing to accept new ideas and to express themselves. People born in the ’70s are more deeply influenced by traditional education, always stressing filial duty and family responsibility.
It sounds like your environment has influenced you a lot. And what about your dad, the one you mentioned?
My dad likes reading, especially books about ideas and thought. He always says reading can broaden your horizons and help you accept new ideas.
What kind of books does he read?
He reads philosophy, psychology, sociology—he reads all of those. He thinks knowledge can make people freer and more able to think independently.
That’s a really rich reading experience. Does he often share these books with you?
Yes, his bookshelf is full of all kinds of books. When I was a kid he often recommended books to me and taught me to think for myself.
Have those books influenced the way you think now?
A lot. I also like reading and I’ve learned to think independently and not be bound by traditional ideas. But when I face family pressure and traditional views, I still feel kind of powerless.
Wow, that really is not easy.
Yeah. Every time there’s a family gathering, facing those traditional ideas and the elders’ expectations, I feel really helpless and sometimes even want to run away.
That sounds really hard. Can you tell me more details about how that feels for you?
Yeah, they’re used to lecturing people and don’t really want to hear other people’s thoughts and voices, especially the voices of the younger generation.
I can understand your frustration. Is there anyone in your family who’s more willing to listen to what you think?
That’s what confuses me. Even though my dad is more open‑minded, when it comes to sexual orientation he might still need time to accept it.
That does sound like a challenge. How do you feel specifically about your dad’s attitude?
I mainly worry that he’ll also be under pressure from the family, and that to keep the peace he might not be willing to openly support me.

That worry is very understandable. I can see you hope your dad will support you, and at the same time you don’t want him to be under too much pressure. How would you like him to handle this so that you could feel more at ease?
Yes, the opinions and pressure from other elders in the family will also affect my dad’s attitude and choices.
I can really see the “70s” and “95” worlds you’re describing, and your language feels very powerful. This conversation lets me feel how capable you are when you express your feelings.
Thank you, that makes me feel some support and understanding. It’s true that expressing my feelings is really important to me.
Mm, I think you express yourself very clearly.
That’s also why, when I’m choosing an online counseling format, I hope I can find something that’s both affordable and effective, that can really let me express and work through my problems.

Online counseling really can offer a platform to express and explore your feelings. You mentioned your dad behaves differently in front of different people—what does that mean to you? Does he care a lot about what others think?
Yes, it means he cares about how the family sees him, and he might sacrifice some of his own thoughts and feelings to keep family harmony. That really matters to me.
It sounds like you feel your dad has made a kind of compromise between family harmony and his personal views.
Yeah, he really is a complicated person. Sometimes I feel it’s hard to figure out what he really thinks.
I understand. The way he goes along with others in front of different people makes him feel complicated and hard to read for you, right?
When he chooses to go along with the family’s opinions, I feel disappointed and helpless, like his support and understanding of me might not be what I hope for.
Do you wish he would argue back with your uncle? Or what would you like your dad to do?
I hope he can express his real thoughts, even if it’s just a mild disagreement, so at least I can see that deep down he supports me.
You feel it’s impossible for him to do that because…?
Because it’s impossible for him to completely ignore the family’s pressure and expectations. He might choose to stay silent and not talk back to the elders.
Why do you think he chooses to handle it that way?
He might worry that family relationships will break down, and be afraid of conflicts within the family, so he chooses to go along.
So when your uncle said those things, how did you respond?
I didn’t react much at the time. I just felt really suffocated inside and chose to stay silent.
You mean it made you feel that at a crucial moment he didn’t stand up for you, right?
Yes, I felt he wasn’t brave enough, that he didn’t stand up for me and didn’t really support me, which left me a bit disappointed.
What made you choose to hold it in?
To keep things looking harmonious on the surface. I didn’t want the family gathering to become awkward and tense, so I chose silence and holding it in.
It seems you’ve given up a lot for the sake of family harmony. What does that choice leave you feeling?
It means the inner pressure has become impossible to hide, and I really can’t bear this emotional burden anymore.
I understand how you feel; long‑term suppression really is hard to bear. Besides keeping the family harmony, what other important feelings are you holding back?
What I care about is the harmony of the family. I don’t want to ruin the whole family atmosphere because of my own feelings, and that’s a kind of compromise I’m making for the family.
That kind of compromise must be hard for you. Could you say more about why you care so much about your dad’s social circle?
Because my dad’s social circle has a big influence on him. He cares about what those people think, and that affects his attitudes and choices, which is very important to me.
I can understand why you care so much about these things. If the relationships with relatives were damaged, what specific impact do you think that would have?
If relationships with relatives broke down, it might intensify conflicts within the family and leave the whole family in a tense and unstable state.
You don’t want to put pressure on your dad or have him be affected. In your dad’s eyes, what kind of son would you be?
Maybe a sensible, considerate son who’s willing to sacrifice his own feelings for the sake of family harmony.
If you imagine that he knew—if he had the chance to hear all this today…
If he knew all this, he might feel heartbroken for me and also reflect on his own behavior and choices, but he might still choose to keep the family harmony.
If he knew you’d rather bear the pressure yourself than damage his social circle, what kind of experience would that be for him?

It might feel very complicated for him. On the one hand he might feel pleased that I understand and compromise for the family, and on the other hand he might feel guilty because he can’t give me more support.
Besides guilt, what else do you think he would feel if he knew?
He might feel happy because I know how to maintain family harmony, but at the same time he’d feel guilty and helpless because he knows I’m under huge inner pressure.
If your dad thought you weren’t being stubborn or insisting on your own way, how would that change how you see your choice to hold it in back then?
I might feel it was a rational choice. For the sake of family harmony and stability, temporarily suppressing my own feelings was a necessary compromise.
I understand what you mean. So how do you see what your dad did at the time?
I might understand him—maybe that was what he thought was the best choice in that situation, even though it disappointed me.
Mm, that really isn’t easy.
Sometimes I can also understand how hard it is for him. Everyone is making some sacrifices for the harmony and stability of the family.
It sounds like you also see him as trying hard for the family, right?
Yes. With fewer conflicts, family relationships don’t get too tense. Even though I feel a bit helpless inside, I can still understand what he does.
It seems you’re really trying to find a balance, even though it’s not easy.
Okay, this conversation has been really enlightening. It’s given me more angles to think about these issues.
I’m wondering whether what we talked about today has been helpful for you. Thank you for being part of this conversation today.
It has helped. Thank you very much for listening and guiding me today. It’s also made my thoughts and feelings about these issues clearer.
I have to say I really like the way you write. There’s a rhythm to it and it’s very precise. Could you share what feels different for you after this session?
Good morning. Um... I can’t really say if I’m good or not.
Good morning. It sounds like you’re having some mixed feelings.
I feel really messy inside, my mood has been complicated all the time.

Could you share what you’ve been thinking about this question?
Yeah. There’s always a lot of friction between us. I feel like he’s getting a bit impatient with me.

It’s actually just so-so, kind of lukewarm. We talk about everyday stuff, but it feels like we never really touch those deeper points in each other’s hearts.
It sounds like you’re running into some difficulties in communicating, and that makes the relationship feel a bit distant.
I’m not sure. Maybe on the surface he seems fine, but I don’t know if inside he has as many doubts and worries as I do.

Sometimes I feel like he’s kind of tired of this relationship, but he doesn’t say it, and I don’t feel comfortable asking too bluntly.
Even though you understand it rationally, emotionally it still feels hard to control.
Yeah. I always hope we can change something and make things better for both of us, but sometimes it feels like the harder I try, the worse it gets.
It sounds like you’re worried about the future of the relationship.
I hope so too. But when it comes to the future, it seems like we’re both a bit unsure.

Not yet. We rarely bring up meeting in person, maybe because we’re both busy.
Mm-hmm. During this time without meeting, how do you two stay in touch?
I’m a bit disappointed, actually. Meeting up should help deepen our feelings, but he doesn’t seem to care much about that.
Mm-hmm. You also mentioned before that you’re afraid you might feel panicky again when you meet.
Yes, I do worry about that. I always get a bit nervous when we meet, and I’m not sure if something unpleasant will happen.
It sounds like you both look forward to and worry a lot about meeting, and all these mixed feelings leave you feeling very uneasy, right?
Sometimes I wonder if I’m overthinking, but those worries just pop up on their own.
That’s very normal. Many people have similar worries when facing something important. Maybe we can explore together: if this meeting turned out differently, how do you think you would feel?
I’d be really happy, but also kind of find it hard to believe. The awkwardness and distance between us almost feel like a habit now.
Mm-hmm, and you don’t know how things will develop. That uncertainty might be making you even more uneasy.
Yeah, sometimes I feel really powerless, like I don’t know what the future will be like.
Mm-hmm. It’s like you’re pushing yourself to take a step forward.
I’ve been trying hard to find a solution. Maybe I really do need to be more decisive and face these problems.

He occasionally sends messages, just some simple greetings. But I feel like it’s really hard for our relationship to go back to being as close as it used to be.
Oh, I see.
Yeah, it’s like a string that’s already broken. You can tie it back together, but it’s no longer whole.
I can understand that. This change leaves you feeling really disappointed, doesn’t it?
It’ll probably be another two years. This period is actually pretty hard to get through.
How have you been coping with these feelings during this time?
Yeah, I’m also afraid that these two years will change a lot of things, maybe even make the distance between us grow.
But it seems like you do have some faith in him, that he’ll be with you.
Yes, I do have that belief, but I can’t guarantee that this belief will always be enough to keep me going.
Mm, I can feel your worry and uncertainty.
Sometimes I feel like I’m walking on a road with no end in sight, not knowing what’s ahead.
You won’t stop until you hit a dead end. In this matter, what do you think that ‘wall’ is for you?
That wall is probably a clear answer, no matter if it’s good or bad.
Mm, I see. You feel that having that conclusion is very important for you.
Yeah, at least then I’d know my efforts in this relationship weren’t for nothing.
That means getting an answer would make you feel that what you’ve given has been acknowledged.
Yes. If I don’t at least try, I might regret it for the rest of my life.
Mm-hmm, at least if you’ve tried, you can feel at peace with yourself.
Yeah, maybe that way I can feel a bit more at ease and not keep getting stuck in the past.
Mm, I understand. If in the end he doesn’t agree, how do you think you would cope with that heartbreak?
I would, I’d definitely be sad. But I think I’d be able to accept it.
It sounds like you’ve already done some mental preparation.
After all, not everything in life goes the way we want.
It seems like you want to give this relationship a sense of closure, is that right?
Yes. I need a clear answer to put a period on this relationship, whether that means continuing or ending it.

It might. That’s why I don’t know if all this waiting is worth it.

Yes, by then maybe everything will already have changed.

So I’m really conflicted right now, I don’t know how to move forward.

Hello, this is my first time using this platform for counseling.

Yeah, recently I’ve been feeling like I have no energy at all, I can’t get myself to do anything. I often feel exhausted and don’t even feel like eating. At night I don’t sleep well either, I often can’t fall asleep, tossing and turning all night with all kinds of messy thoughts in my head.

It’s been almost half a year, roughly since I realized I was gradually being sidelined at work. From then on, this feeling just kept getting worse.
That’s quite a long time. Has it had a negative impact on your work, family, or social life?

Yes, this state has affected my work efficiency and also made my relationships with family and friends tense. I’ve become unwilling to socialize, and my relationships with colleagues and friends have faded a lot.
Mm. It sounds like this feeling has been going on for a while. Can you tell me more about what things were like half a year ago? For example, did anything happen then that really mattered to you?

Half a year ago, my boss found out that I was planning to go abroad, and then he gradually stopped assigning me important tasks. At first I could understand it and tried to prove my value, but little by little I felt I was being ignored. Plus my coworkers also started to distance themselves, and I increasingly felt isolated. That made me really sad and disappointed.
Mm, what do you think it is that you regret?

What I regret is that I told my boss about my plan to go abroad without thinking it through. Even though I was really looking forward to a new life and study opportunities, I didn’t consider that it would have such a negative impact on my current job.
Could you say more specifically? What was the situation like at that time?

Right, at that time I was really excited and felt my future was full of possibilities, so I told my boss. I didn’t expect that afterwards he would stop trusting me and wouldn’t want me involved in important projects anymore. I feel like I lost opportunities to grow, and that was a big blow to me.
It sounds like this has had a big impact on you. How are your emotions and your state now?

I didn’t quit, I was just marginalized. But this feeling is almost the same as if I had resigned, it’s really hard to bear. Every day when I go to work I can’t get myself going, and I keep feeling like my presence has no value.
I hear you, that must feel really hard. Over the past six months, how have your emotions changed?

Yeah, in these six months my mood has been pretty unstable and has become very negative. I feel like my career development is stuck, which puts a lot of pressure on me and makes it hard for me to feel happy any day.
I can understand your pressure and the negative feelings. Have you thought about how to cope with or improve this situation?
No, I’m not planning to change jobs, because I still plan to go abroad. And even though my current position is easy, I’m not happy at all. I feel like I’m wasting my time.
I understand. Even if the work is easy, if the content doesn’t bring a sense of achievement or satisfaction, it can really feel like a waste of time.

Yes, I’ve also tried to stay in touch with my former colleagues, but they’re all very busy and I don’t want to bother them. And my current coworkers, because of my plans, don’t really seem to want to get close to me either, which makes me feel very lonely.
It sounds like you care a lot about relationships with colleagues, and now this kind of cold environment makes you feel lonely, is that right?

Maybe it’s because I really hope to gain recognition and grow at work, and now this feeling of being left out makes me feel very disappointed and helpless. And of course there’s pressure too, I’m afraid I won’t be able to achieve anything before I leave the company.

That feeling of being left out is indeed very hard, especially when you’re hoping for recognition and growth. We can explore together how to cope with these emotions and this pressure, how does that sound?
My physical health has been affected a lot, mainly with eating and sleeping. After binge eating my stomach always feels uncomfortable, and the insomnia leaves me drained every day.
These eating and sleeping issues sound like they’re affecting you a lot. Have you tried anything to ease these symptoms?
No, this is my first time trying counseling. I’m hoping to find some ways to make myself feel a bit better.
Got it. We’ll explore methods that suit you and help you gradually improve your current state.

Yes, even though I didn’t actually resign, my mood feels pretty much like after quitting. My main problem now is how to regain my enthusiasm for work, improve my state, and not feel so down and powerless.
