I hope you can give me some advice, like how to get him to quit these bad habits, or how to rebuild our communication.

Thank you for directly telling me your expectations and needs. I can offer some strategies and suggestions, but that would need to be after I understand your specific situation better. Every person and every family has their own unique circumstances and ways of coping.
I understand, and I’m willing to try to open up so you can understand my situation better.
We can start by talking about times when the communication and interaction between you were good. Could you share some experiences when you were able to communicate effectively and solve problems?
When we first got married, although there were also frictions, he cared about me a lot. The happiness I felt back then has made me keep not wanting to give up on this marriage.
When you’ve been hurt, how have you supported yourself to keep going?
I always tell myself that these difficulties are temporary, and that we still have a chance to welcome a better life together.
So you give yourself strength by telling yourself these difficulties are temporary, and that helps you keep going, is that right?
Yes, that’s how I’ve been encouraging myself all along, placing my hope in the future.
I can understand. You really are very strong, and you’ve been trying hard to overcome all kinds of difficulties. This process must not have been easy. What are the things that have disappointed you?
Every time, I expect him to change and to work hard together with me, but the result always disappoints me.
What kind of hope are you referring to?
I hope he can quit smoking and drinking, spend less time playing mahjong, and spend more time with me, especially at this critical time when we’re preparing for pregnancy.
Have you tried discussing these things with him? How does he respond?
Yes, I’ve been trying to communicate with him, but I feel like he simply doesn’t want to listen to me, and there’s been no improvement at all.
Your hopes, or the way you expect things to be—would you be willing to describe that to me?
I hope that after work we can cook together, talk, exercise, and enjoy each other’s company, instead of him always being absorbed in mahjong, smoking, and drinking.
You just mentioned that he’s absorbed in mahjong, smoking, and drinking. Are there any particular reasons, such as pressure in life or work?
Yes. After his business failed before, his mood has been very low. I can understand his pressure, but those are not reasons for him to be immersed in these bad habits.

I can sense that in this situation, you feel pushed away and helpless. This must make you very sad, because you’ve been doing your best to take care of the family and hoping to get through this difficult time.
Yes, I’ve been trying hard to take care of our family and hoping we can get through this difficult time, but he isn’t willing to face these problems with me.
When you heard these explanations from him, how did you respond at the time?
I told him I understood his pressure and was willing to get through this with him, but I hoped he could change some behaviors. But he always just brushes me off.
Mm-hmm.
Sometimes I really don’t know what else I can do. He always makes me feel like my efforts are all in vain.
If it were me, I might have the same reaction as you.
Really? Sometimes I even wonder if I’m being too much, but hearing you say that makes me feel a little better. At least my feelings are reasonable.
This has been buried in your heart all along. I feel that deep down, you really wish this weren’t true. It’s so painful.
Yes. I don’t want us to come to this point. I really hope he can change, and that we can become better together.
I can understand your feelings. I hope that through our conversation, you can find ways to help yourself feel a little more at ease.
I don’t know. I really don’t know whether he can change. Sometimes I feel like he has already given up on us, given up on this family.
I can feel that you care a lot about the future of this family.
Oh, there’s no particular reason. I just suddenly thought of it.
Actually, what kind of answer are you hoping I’ll give you?
I guess I’m hoping you can tell me whether he might still change, and whether our relationship can still be saved.
What do you think my answer would change? I understand that, facing all of this, Qiqi, you really feel helpless. So you really hope someone can help you take a look at it and analyze what to do.
Yes, I really hope someone can give me some guidance, so I know what to do to save our marriage.

We may have the opportunity to make changes together, but the troubles inside us often can’t be resolved in one conversation. The complexity and conflicts in life can really be painful. I understand that you really want someone to quickly help you think through strategies or do something to make an effort. If you’re willing to wait a little longer, and give both yourself and the counselor a bit of time, there may be a chance for something different. What do you think?
I’m willing to try. I’m willing to give myself and our relationship some time, and I also hope we can find some effective methods.
That’s okay.
Thank you for being willing to help me.

A counseling session is usually about 50 minutes, but because there are still some things we haven’t finished talking about, and I also sense that Qiqi still has some emotions weighing on her, if you’re willing, we can extend the time a bit. How are you feeling now, Qiqi? I sense that you have some thoughts.
I’m feeling a little better now. I feel like I’m not completely alone and helpless, and that there is still someone willing to listen to me.
At the moment, there is no charge.
Okay, then can I keep talking with you a bit more? I feel like I still have a lot I want to say.
You asked me for some of my views earlier, but I didn’t respond directly. That may have made you feel a bit disappointed, right?
Yes. Sometimes I hope I can get more direct advice, maybe because I feel too anxious inside, but I understand that this needs to happen step by step.

I understand your feelings. Sometimes wanting to get advice right away is a very natural reaction. The main goal of counseling is to help you sort through your emotions, thoughts, and behaviors. Through this process, we can slowly make some changes. If this is not quite what you expected, I’m sorry that I disappointed you. But please trust that I have been paying attention to your concerns, and I care about your views and feelings.
It’s okay, I understand. You’ve already helped me a lot, letting me release the emotions I’ve been holding inside.

If the conversation just now didn’t meet your expectations, that’s also very normal, especially since we’re communicating through text. Sometimes there will inevitably be gaps in how words are interpreted. What’s important is that you can try your best to express your thoughts and feelings.
Okay. I’ll try to express my needs more directly in the future. Thank you for understanding me.

Of course you would feel anxious. I really understand that feeling. It’s like, after finally finding a place to let things out, and the other person has a professional background, of course you would hope to get some advice. I understand. Thank you for expressing yourself so sincerely.
Thank you for being willing to listen to what’s in my heart and for understanding my feelings. This really means a lot to me.

I’m glad I’ve been able to help you. Finally, I can offer a few small methods. But I’d also like to know, is there anything else you want to tell me in this conversation? You can say anything you’d like.

Right now I really hope I can find some ways to help my husband realize how serious the problem is, and to truly start taking action to change, instead of always staying at the stage of superficially agreeing with me.

Mm, I actually feel that because of this matter, you really have a lot of hurt and sadness, and it really hasn’t been easy. This has probably affected your ability to keep communicating with him. Maybe we can first take care of your own emotions. Then, when it comes to communication, once your mood has settled and you’re able to take good care of yourself, whether you talk face-to-face directly or communicate indirectly through writing or messages, you’ll at least feel more grounded. What do you think?
Yes, I also think I need to adjust my emotions first, so I can have more strength to face the communication and challenges that come next.

It really is difficult. This is such a huge blow. About regulating your own emotions, I was also thinking just now that perhaps I can recommend a few practical small methods. Of course, this varies from person to person, and it’s just a reference. First, I remember you said that when it’s quiet, it’s easy for you to think a lot. Maybe you can try to be with those thoughts and feel them. When it’s quiet, you can try meditation exercises. Following guided instructions can help you calm yourself down. Second, keep an emotion journal—just record your emotions and try to label them, such as when I felt what emotion, whether this emotion seems positive or negative to me, and whether it is intense or mild. You can write it in the notes app on your phone or on paper; either is good. We have the opportunity to become the master of our emotions, even if it’s just by seeing them. Third, try self-encouragement. Before bed every day, write down specific things you can encourage yourself about. Qiqi, you really have already done very well. You are a very brave person. That’s what I’m thinking of. To speak about the hardships in life is absolutely not an easy thing; you really have a lot of courage. Is there anything else you want to tell me in this counseling session?

I’ll try these methods, and I hope they can help my emotions stabilize. Actually, I also want to know, if he never changes, how should I face this sense of powerlessness? Should I keep trying, or consider other options?

Facing this kind of powerlessness is indeed very hard to deal with, especially when you’ve put in a lot of effort but haven’t seen corresponding change. We can further explore some strategies you can take, or think through other options. However, since our time today is probably about up, perhaps we can discuss this issue in more detail in our next session. Thank you today, Qiqi, for sincerely telling me all of this and for being willing to stay close to your own feelings. I hope today’s counseling can help you, even if just a little. Shall we pause here for now, okay?
Okay. Thank you. Today’s conversation has really helped me a lot.
You’re very welcome.
Thank you. I’ll come back and talk with you again.

Of course. Next time we can continue talking, as long as I have an available counseling slot. I hope you can fill out two counseling outcome evaluation questionnaires. This can help us better understand your real feelings and improve the counseling that follows.

Sigh, I really feel like I’ve had enough of this company. I’ve put in so much effort, and in the end I’m still not appreciated. My boss doesn’t appreciate it at all. I really don’t know why I should keep working this hard.
Good evening. How has this week been?
Sigh, this week has been awful. I keep feeling like I’m wasting my effort.
It sounds like this week has been really hard for you, and you feel your efforts haven’t been recognized, is that right?
Yeah, I just feel especially powerless, and it feels really unfair. I was already planning to resign in two weeks, but every day I’m still being suffocated by all kinds of tasks.
I can understand that sense of powerlessness. It’s really not easy facing so much pressure.

Especially last night. I was already getting ready to rest, and that supervisor still sent me a document and asked me to give revision suggestions. It was so annoying. My first reaction was to deal with it on Monday, but I still couldn’t help opening it to take a look.
It seems like this kind of situation really bothers you, and even disrupts your time to rest, right?

Even though I feel this company isn’t worth it, it’s like there’s this inertia that makes me finish the tasks and immediately meet other people’s expectations. And them? They don’t respect my efforts at all.
It sounds like at work, you try hard to meet other people’s expectations, but you don’t feel the corresponding respect, and that leaves you feeling very frustrated.
Right. I keep feeling like my system has been disrupted. I was interrupted so late last night, and then I woke up very early today, and I’ve been really irritated.
It sounds like you didn’t get to rest well last night, and that’s made you feel very irritable, right?
Being interrupted like this every day is really unbearable. It feels like the pressure is getting bigger and bigger.
It seems like you’re feeling a lot of pressure. This kind of disruption has a big impact on both your mood and your physical state, doesn’t it?
Honestly, I haven’t had any good way to let it out lately. I just try to relax as much as I can, but I still feel tired.
I see. Is it that even though you’re trying to relax, it doesn’t seem to help much, and you still feel tired and under a lot of pressure?
Sometimes it really is hard to fall asleep, and I wake up early too. But yesterday, aside from being disturbed, I actually slept pretty well.
It seems that last night’s interruption was especially upsetting for you. The usual fatigue and pressure may also be affecting the quality of your sleep.
Mm, yeah. I always feel like the work is never done. Clearly the other colleagues don’t have as much to do as I do, but they seem very relaxed.

It sounds like your workload is heavy, and that makes you feel very weighed down. And seeing your colleagues in a more relaxed state may make it feel even more unfair and increase your pressure, right?
No, I didn’t work overtime on the weekend. Luckily I got one day of rest.
It sounds like your usual work really is very busy, so having a day to rest is not easy.
Maybe it’s because I’m usually too efficient. I always feel like the boss is more willing to give the important tasks to me.
You feel that your boss trusts you more and gives you the important tasks.
Sigh, maybe it’s because I’ve always been pretty reliable. But as a result, I end up under more pressure.
Because you’re reliable, you’re trusted, but that also makes you feel more pressure.
Sometimes I really feel like I do too much, and instead no one appreciates it.
It sounds like you feel you’ve done a lot, but haven’t received the recognition you deserve, and that makes you feel very disappointed.
Sticky notes are somewhat useful, but the problem is that tasks just keep getting added.
Mm, I can understand what’s troubling you. Even though you’re trying hard, sometimes you still feel a lot of pressure. We can look again at how to better manage these constantly increasing tasks.
Yes. But even so, they still come and rush me.
I understand. You’re saying that even when you’re busy, they still come over to urge you, is that right?
Right. No matter how I arrange things, someone always interrupts my plan.
It sounds like these interruptions make it hard for you to focus, and it feels very frustrating, right?
The biggest problem is that I can’t concentrate. I’m always being interrupted, and the tasks still don’t get finished.
Mm, I understand. That must make you feel like your work progress is being affected a lot, right?
And working overtime doesn’t solve the problem either.
So if you don’t work overtime, you worry the tasks won’t get finished, right?
If I don’t work overtime, the tasks won’t get finished, and I might get criticized by the boss.
If you’re constantly being rushed, how does that make you feel? And if you were able to have a block of uninterrupted time to work, what do you think would change?
If I’m constantly being rushed, I’ll feel a lot of pressure. If I insist on not breaking up large blocks of time, the work might not get done on time.
It sounds like you feel a lot of pressure from being constantly pushed.
If I were thick-skinned enough, maybe I wouldn’t care about other people rushing me. But I always feel like that’s not the fundamental way to solve the problem.
You feel that ignoring the pressure from others isn’t a real solution. Could you say more about what you’re worried about?
Maybe I could try doing that, but I’m still worried the result won’t be ideal, and the boss will be even more dissatisfied.
I understand your worry, that trying something that doesn’t work might make your boss even more dissatisfied.
Maybe it would reduce the pressure in the short term, but over time, there might still be a lot of unfinished tasks piling up.
You’re worried that a short-term strategy could lead to a backlog of work in the long run.
After that, maybe my colleagues and boss would all have complaints about me, and the environment would get even worse.
It seems you’re worried this situation would affect your relationships with your colleagues and boss, and make the work environment worse.
Yeah. This pressure comes from every direction, and it really feels awful.
Yes. Earlier you mentioned you haven’t talked with your supervisor yet. You could check with your supervisor about work priorities, what’s urgent and what’s less urgent.
Mm, that’s one way. Maybe I can try talking to him about what I’m struggling with.
Communication is indeed a good start, and it can help clarify which tasks need to be handled first.
Right. It feels like it will never be finished. The more I do, the more there is.
That feeling is very common, and many people have similar struggles. We can discuss some ways to manage time and priorities.
Yes, I’ve already felt that very deeply.
You mentioned that what you need is not to spend your whole life working in a muddled way.
Right. I hope I can do meaningful work, instead of always being held back by these trivial tasks.

So, have you specifically analyzed which tasks are valuable to you personally? For example, which tasks are good for your career development and salary growth, and which ones don’t really offer growth?
Mm, some projects really can train my abilities and help me grow. But more of them are those mechanical, repetitive tasks.
I understand.
Those repetitive tasks feel like they’re wasting my time when I do them.
Could you say more about what a day looks like for you?
If I only did those kinds of tasks, maybe my efficiency would improve, and I’d be more motivated too.
If you could do more of that kind of work, what impact would it have on your overall work state?
If the tasks don’t get finished, I’m afraid the boss will blame me, and maybe my performance evaluation will be affected.
I understand. Then what kind of work do you think could give you more growth and improve your chances of promotion and a raise?
If I did more of this meaningful work, it might increase my chances of promotion and a raise.
That sounds like the outcome you’re hoping for, right?
Yes, that’s the goal I’ve been pursuing all along.
It sounds like this is a very important goal for you.
It’s better than endlessly doing those trivial tasks here.
You feel those trivial tasks are very meaningless, right?
Right. At least this way I can see my own progress, and I won’t feel like I’m wasting time.
You hope to see your own progress by choosing meaningful work, and that would make you feel more fulfilled.
Right. Even though this might cause some dissatisfaction among colleagues, it’s a choice that benefits my future.
That’s understandable. As you make decisions for your future, you also have to face some challenges and friction with colleagues.
If my colleagues aren’t happy, there may be some friction, but so what? I have to consider my own development first.
Indeed, sometimes for your own development, you have to face some pressure in interpersonal relationships. How are you thinking about this situation?
If my colleagues aren’t happy, there may be some friction, but so what? I have to consider my own development first.
It sounds like you already have a clear idea and a strategy for how to respond. That’s really good.
Yeah. If I can keep going like this, maybe there will be more opportunities.
It sounds like you have some hopes for the future.
Right. At least this way there’s hope, and I won’t stay trapped in meaningless work all the time.
Could you talk about what kind of work you feel is meaningful?
Because only in this way can I feel my own value, instead of constantly spending time like a frog being slowly boiled in warm water.
You hope to feel your own value through work.
It’s hard to say, but if I keep doing those repetitive tasks, that definitely won’t work. I still need to choose meaningful work.
I understand. Repetitive tasks make you feel that life lacks growth and change.
Yes. At least this way I can have hope, and I won’t feel like everything is wasting my youth.
I hope you can find work that makes you feel fulfilled and hopeful.
It feels like the direction is clearer this way, and I won’t feel so lost.
Then let’s stop here for today. I encourage you to prioritize the work tasks that have a positive impact on your growth.
Okay, I’ll keep this suggestion in mind. Thank you for your help.
Thank you for your trust. I look forward to seeing more gains next time we meet. See you Monday.
Good afternoon, Shui Shui. Long time no see.
Long time no see. How have you been lately?
Mm, lately I feel like there have been some changes in my emotions. It seems like I don’t feel happy as easily as I used to.
You mentioned some changes in your emotions. Can you say more specifically what those changes are like?
Actually... they’re not entirely good changes. I’m feeling more and more of this indescribable sense of powerlessness.
I can understand that. Your feelings may be a bit complicated, right?

I used to always feel like I was the cheerful one in a group, the one who could make everyone laugh. But now it’s getting harder and harder to be around people, especially when I’m facing other people’s negative emotions. I feel really at a loss.
It sounds like the way you relate to people has changed a lot for you. What impact do you feel these changes have had on you?
I feel like I’ve become more indifferent. When coworkers or friends express their feelings, I can’t empathize at all, and I even keep wanting to avoid it.
What is the indifference you’re feeling like for you? Could you say a little more?
It feels like I’m looking at the world through a layer of film, like everything isn’t real.
It sounds like your feelings have changed somewhat. How does this sense of things becoming unreal feel to you?
Honestly, I’m still adjusting. But sometimes my own indifference scares me too. I’m afraid I’ll stay like this forever.
It’s understandable that you feel scared while adjusting to this change. Can you say more specifically what things make you feel this way?
For example, yesterday I watched a video. I thought I wouldn’t react that much, but halfway through, I couldn’t help crying for a long time.
Watching that video brought up a big emotional reaction for you. Could you share what made you cry for so long?
It made me feel a lot of pain inside, like some feelings I had originally been trying to cover up all surged out at once, but I didn’t know how to deal with those emotions.
That sounds truly painful. When facing these emotions, you feel troubled, right?
Yes. It’s a bit like being forced to face the emotions I don’t want to face. It’s really painful.
I understand. It really does feel very difficult for you when you face these emotions.
Yes, but I’ve never dared to think this way... because I’m afraid that if I accept these emotional needs, I’ll become more fragile.
When you mentioned acceptance and not expecting earlier, is this the part you mean?
Yes. I’m trying not to expect others to understand my emotional needs anymore, but honestly, it’s really hard.
Hearing you say that, I can feel your sadness.
Actually, I’m very sad too. I’ve thought many times about why I became like this, and what exactly happened in the past that made me so afraid to face my own emotions.
I can sense that you’ve gone through difficult and painful memories in this process. We can explore some ways together to gradually ease the distress you’re feeling.
Mm, the atmosphere and experiences in my family really have been hard for me, but sometimes I feel like I’m not qualified to complain about these things.
When we feel emotions that are too much to bear, avoiding them can sometimes be a way of protecting ourselves. In your mind, what would truly resolving the problem look like?
Truly resolving the problem might require me and my family to open up to each other, but I’ve never had the courage to really face them. I’m afraid I’ll break down even more.

Facing the reality of the situation may take a lot of courage. Many people find that when they’re able to truly face their own feelings, it often brings inner changes, and those changes can gradually affect their real life. Even though this isn’t easy, perhaps we can explore this process together.
I understand, but whenever I think about doing these things, I feel very afraid.
Mm-hmm, I understand.
Sometimes I hope I can build up a little courage, even if it’s just to tell them some of my feelings. But like you said, it really is hard.

Yes, this courage is built up and grows little by little. I still remember one time when you shared with me your experience of mustering the courage to change seats. I also respect that there are parts of you that need to stay hidden. Those parts may not be ready to come out and meet people yet, so let them stay hidden for now.
Thank you for your understanding and patience. Sometimes I feel like I’m really too cowardly.
I’m really glad you can share these feelings. Let’s take it slowly together, okay?
I did have some impulsive thoughts before, but now it’s a little better.
Mm, I understand. Have you still been having thoughts like that recently?
Occasionally, but you don’t need to worry. I’ll try my best to control myself and find some ways to adjust my emotions.

Thank you for being considerate. I can feel that. What I’m mainly concerned about is your safety and health. We can explore some ways together to help you cope with these emotions better. This kind of change really does take time; it won’t happen all at once.
Mm, I also know this takes time and patience.
But every time I see you come online and share some little everyday things with me, I feel happy. I hope you’re truly doing well, and that you’re still living your life as best you can.
I’ll try to keep sharing with you. This is also some of the support and comfort I can find.
I’m very willing to listen to you talk about these things, if you’re willing.
Okay. I’ll try to share more with you, and I hope this can help me find some direction.
Would this kind of understanding be helpful to you? Sometimes sensing yourself may bring up pain, uneasiness, and feelings of wanting to escape.
It would. Sensing myself really is quite painful, but I know this step is necessary.
If you have uncomfortable feelings, you can tell me anytime, and we can stop. Yes.
Okay, thank you for your concern. I’ll pay attention to that.
That protection is very important. If pain can’t be avoided, expressing your feelings is also our right.
Thank you. I’ll try not to keep suppressing myself when I feel bad, and find some people I can trust to talk to.
Mm-hmm. You can also try patting yourself on the shoulder now and telling yourself, you’ve already done really well. You were able to be so honest today, and I really admire your courage.
Thank you for your support all along. I also feel that being able to talk about these things with you gives me strength.
It goes both ways, I think. It’s an honor to be trusted by you. If there’s anything I can do, please let me know.
Okay, I will. Wishing you all the best too. See you next time!
Wishing you all the best too. See you next time!
Hello, Xiaotian. I’ve been feeling very depressed lately. I’ve been looking for more than half a year and still haven’t been able to find a counselor in a stable way. I don’t know what to do.
Hello, Awen. I really appreciate you continuing to come and talk about these things. That’s not easy at all.

I love comparing myself with others. It feels like there are two people inside me fighting—one wants to relax, and the other really wants to become better. I don’t doubt my need for counseling, but it’s hard to find a counselor who makes me feel comfortable.
It sounds like you really care a lot about the conflict inside you, and you very much want to find a suitable counselor to help you. I can understand this struggle.
Actually, none of that matters. What matters is the anxiety and pressure inside me. I have to find a counselor who can help me.
I understand how you feel. Anxiety and pressure have been troubling you for a long time. Can you say more specifically where these anxiety and pressure mainly come from?

I started looking for a counselor in the summer after my third year of high school, but it was never stable. The counselors on those low-cost platforms lacked experience, or communication with me didn’t go smoothly. Their manner or way of speaking made me uncomfortable.

I can understand that feeling. Finding a suitable counselor who makes you feel comfortable really isn’t easy. From what you’ve described, I can see your effort and persistence in this area. Let’s continue exploring how to better cope with these anxieties and pressures.
Whenever I run into this kind of situation, I feel even more stressed. I also blame myself a bit, always wondering if I’m being too picky.
I understand how you feel. It’s a very normal reaction for pressure to increase in this kind of situation. Can you talk a little more about your self-blame?

Later I tried a few career planners, but they couldn’t understand my psychological issues. After I started university, I found a counselor on campus, but she also made me feel distant, not gentle enough.
It sounds like the counselors you met made you feel some discomfort and distance. I can understand how troubling this has been for you.
Exactly. My feelings are very important. Finding a suitable counselor really isn’t easy.
Yes, finding a counselor who is right for you really is important.
So I really hope I can find a regular counselor who suits me, instead of constantly changing.
I can understand how you feel. Frequently changing counselors really can bring you a lot of distress.
Actually, I also know that my standards may be quite high. Every time I meet with a counselor, if something feels off inside, I don’t want to keep seeing them anymore.

That’s very normal. Finding a counselor who can make you feel comfortable and trusting is a process in itself. If you’re willing, we can keep exploring this issue and see what approaches might help you.
That sounds good. I also hope that through our joint efforts, we can solve my problems. I’ve been looking for someone like this all along.
I have a graduate degree in psychology, and I’ve had hospital internship experience and training, with five years of practical experience. Is there anything else you’d like to know?
That makes you sound very professional. Then can I keep talking with you about what’s been troubling me?
Of course. I’m very willing to listen to what’s troubling you. Please tell me about your feelings and thoughts.
Okay. I hope that through our conversations, I can gradually find the root of the problem and reduce my anxiety and pressure.
I understand how you feel. Let’s work together and see what kinds of issues we can identify, and look for ways to address them.
That would be great. Having more ways to communicate might make me feel closer.
Yes, right. Building good communication is very important for our counseling process.
But right now, I really need some concrete help and advice, especially when it comes to finding a suitable counselor.
I understand what you need. We can start from here and see what practical ways might help you.
Yes. My condition is getting worse and worse now, and there isn’t much time. I hope I can start effective counseling as soon as possible.
I understand. Your feelings are important. We can explore your current situation together and look for solutions that suit you.
I understand. I hope the new features can bring more convenience.
Mm, I understand your expectations. Let’s focus on your concerns now. You mentioned your current state just now—can you say more specifically what has been happening?
I understand. Settings and rules are important. Then I’ll follow the official account and hope I can find more useful information.
Yes, the setting and rules of psychological counseling are indeed very important. As for your situation, we can explore it more deeply here. I hope our conversation can help you.
I understand what you mean. Thank you for the suggestion. I’ll take a look at “Xinling Research Institute” and hope it will be helpful.
You’re welcome. If you have any questions or need further help, remember you can come to me anytime.
I understand, thank you.
Mm-hmm, you’re welcome.
Good afternoon.
How have you been lately?

Yes, but the result is that I’m especially exhausted.

Yes. Every time I have to struggle with it for a long time, and it’s really painful.

You’re very sensitive to other people’s feelings, and at the same time you long for your own feelings to be valued.

Mm-hmm, take your time. I’m listening.

Yes. I hope to experience a relationship purely, but in practice I’m always limited by my patterns of thinking.

Mm, I feel this part really does need deeper exploration, because it runs through my attitudes and behaviors toward all relationships.

Yes, but sometimes I also wonder whether this survival rule has made me more isolated.

Sometimes she shows a kind of helpless and disappointed expression, especially when I push her away.
It seems like a disappointed expression gave you that signal.
Yes. Her eyes and expression make me feel her lack of understanding and disappointment.
When you sensed her disappointment, what about your own feelings?
I feel guilty, like I’ve done something wrong, but at the same time I feel powerless to change it.
It sounds like there are a lot of complicated feelings inside you.
I know my behavior doesn’t match her expectations, but I’m also not sure how to find a balance.
What do you think your expectations and her expectations are in this relationship?
I hope we can be like partners, facing life’s challenges together, rather than one person being completely dependent on the other.

Yes. I always feel like my needs don’t really matter, and I’m afraid that if I say them out loud, other people will think I’m being too much or selfish.

Yes. When I was little, it seemed like every time I tried to express my needs, they weren’t accepted. Instead, I was blamed or ignored.

Yes. Whenever I try to express my needs, I unconsciously think of those childhood experiences, and then I feel like what I’m doing is wrong, and very shameful.

Yes. Whenever I try to express my needs, I unconsciously think of those childhood experiences, and then I feel like what I’m doing is wrong, and very shameful.

For you, what does relying on someone else mean?

It sounds like what you’re talking about is a sense of ease and being understood.
Yes. It’s that feeling of being able to express my feelings and needs with peace of mind, without having to worry about being ignored or blamed.

Yes. When I run into difficulties and conflict, having someone willing to stand by my side, support and encourage me, instead of leaving me to face it alone—that, to me, is a kind of reliance.

I’m curious. I can feel your strong love for your dad, and your strong wish to receive some emotional response and connection from him. Have you ever expressed these things to your dad very directly and clearly?

Lately I’ve been feeling really irritable, because I’m living in the dorm with people born after 1995, and I feel like our lifestyles and habits are really different.
Mm-hmm.
The atmosphere in our dorm isn’t very good. I can’t really talk with them, and I always feel uncomfortable.
It sounds like you’re feeling really upset in the dorm, and that must be very hard for you.
But the teacher isn’t willing to change my dorm. He said the people in that dorm already have their graduation certificates, and I don’t yet, so it would be more complicated.
Mm, I understand. Hearing the teacher say that may have left you feeling confused and disappointed, is that right?
Exactly. I feel like the whole plan has been disrupted again, and I don’t know how to get along with them. It’s really bothering me.
It sounds like you’re facing a big challenge in adapting to a new environment, and having your plans disrupted is making you feel very anxious, right?
Yes. I thought that since they were just interns, things would be a bit simpler, but it’s actually become more complicated.
It seems like things are much more complicated than you expected, and that’s making you feel a bit exhausted and overwhelmed.
Because I feel like a new environment would be more helpful for growth and learning, and I could come into contact with more opportunities.
Okay. A new environment can indeed bring many opportunities, and at the same time it comes with some challenges. Your original intention was to grow and learn better.
I really have tried to consider everyone’s feelings, but now I realize I also need more care and understanding.
Hearing you say this makes me feel that you’re very considerate and understanding. Those teachers must be very grateful that you made this decision.
I hope so, but I really do feel a bit wronged inside.
I can understand how you feel. This kind of situation really can make someone feel wronged. You’re truly very brave.
Thank you for the compliment, but being brave doesn’t mean I’m not tired.

That’s true. Being brave and feeling exhausted don’t conflict with each other. The situation you’re in now may require more adjusting and overcoming, but that doesn’t mean your feelings aren’t important.
You’re right. I’ve been through a lot of challenges, but this time still feels especially hard.

Your sensitivity and thoughtfulness may have led you to take on more responsibility than others. You’ve been at the school the longest, and you have a sense of responsibility, which may have made you overlook your own needs when making decisions for your colleagues.
I do sometimes feel like I’m carrying too much and can’t focus on my own things.
I understand. That sense of burden really can make it hard to focus on your own needs.
Sometimes I really feel a lot of pressure, especially since the people around me are so much older than me. Communicating with them is very difficult.
It sounds like you feel a bit lonely when getting along with your colleagues, and like you don’t have much in common to talk about, right?
Not exactly. It’s just that I simply feel like we don’t have a common language, and I feel very lonely inside.
I understand. That feeling really is hard to sit with. Have you tried sharing some of your interests or experiences with your colleagues, to see if there might be common topics?
That’s a good idea. I’ll try asking my colleagues.
Good. If anything is difficult or you feel you need help, you can talk to me anytime. Also, maybe joining an activity you like could help you meet new friends who share your interests.
I hope this experience can make me stronger, though right now it’s really hard to get through.
I can sense your strength and determination. Adapting to a new environment really isn’t easy, but you’re already doing very well. Remember, you’re not alone. We’ll be here with you.
Thank you for your support. It really makes me feel much better.

You got through that frightening medical exam, and three years ago when you went to your previous school, you were able to adapt very well too. I believe you must have many wonderful strengths. Remember to celebrate every small step of progress you make.
Hearing you say that, I do feel like I’ve grown quite a lot.
That’s really great! I believe you’ll become more and more skilled at work too.
I hope the days ahead can go a little more smoothly.

At the beginning, you were already prepared for the early stage to be hard, but during the process, what we often feel more is the pressure rather than the gains. Still, the decision you made back then was to prepare for a better future.
Yes, even though it’s very hard right now, I believe things will get better in the future.
Sometimes we need to give up some things in order to gain others. You’ve already been very brave; it’s just that you may need to keep going for a while longer.
I’ll do my best to keep going. Thank you for your encouragement.
If you keep going, you’ll see the light.
With your encouragement, I feel like I have strength again.

Yes. Right now, you’re also making plans for yourself, and you don’t need to think too much about others. We’re about out of time for this session, so let’s stop here for today, okay? You’re really doing very well.
Okay, thank you. I feel much better.
You’re welcome. I’m very glad to hear you’re feeling much better. Keep holding on to this positive state.
Hello, counselor Xiaotian. Please call me Lemon.

Okay, hello, Lemon. Do you have enough time right now? Our conversation will last 50 minutes. I invite you to find a comfortable and safe place to have our talk. When you’re ready, you can let me know.
Okay, I’m in my dorm, and it’s fairly quiet. We can start.
I saw that you wrote self-exploration, emotional distress, and academic difficulties as your main concerns. What would you mainly like to talk about today?
Mm, academic difficulties are something I’ve been thinking about a lot recently. Especially procrastination and avoiding studying—it makes me feel very confused and anxious.
Mm-hmm, it sounds like this has been troubling you. Maybe you could give an example or describe a situation, to help me better understand what’s going on for you.

For example, recently I’ve had assignments due for several classes, and I always put them off until the last moment before starting. I clearly know that starting earlier would make things much easier, but I just can’t take action, and in the end the quality of the work isn’t good.
I understand. This situation must be very frustrating for you. I noticed you mentioned the problem of “having difficulty starting.” What feelings are behind that?
Yes, I always feel that if I start and don’t do it well, people will laugh at me. I’m afraid others will judge me badly, so instead I don’t dare to take the first step.

It sounds like you care about how others see you, and you’re afraid of the negative evaluation that might come with failure. This seems to be pulling at you and making it hard for you to start. Do you feel that way?
Mm, that’s exactly it. I want to change my current situation, but I’m also afraid of failing, afraid of being mocked or looked down on.
Mm, that may be one possible reason, and you’ve analyzed it quite clearly. So, Lemon, what kind of evaluation do you hope to receive?
Actually, I hope I can be recognized by others, especially the people I care about. I hope they can see my effort and give me positive feedback.
I understand. You hope to be recognized and affirmed by the people around you.
Yes, I always hope I can do my best and reach a perfect standard. But sometimes this pursuit of perfection makes me afraid to try new things.

I’m thinking of the perfectionism you mentioned at the beginning. Maybe, maybe, as you said, you want to reach that ideal version you have in mind. If you’re not sure you can do it well or receive a good evaluation, then you simply “run away” for a bit.
Yes, sometimes it feels like if I know I can’t do it well, then I might as well not do it. At least then I don’t have to face failure.
I understand. The “running away” you mentioned means that when facing uncertainty, you choose not to try.

This avoidance isn’t just about assignments. There are also many everyday things. For example, communicating with classmates, participating in club activities, and so on—I also procrastinate or avoid them.
Can you say more specifically what kinds of things you procrastinate on or avoid?
For example, reviewing for exams, finishing assignments, replying to professors’ emails. In daily life, sometimes I also procrastinate on small things like doing laundry and cleaning.
From what you’re saying, the impact of procrastination is mainly on your academics. I’m also curious about areas like relationships, emotions, daily life, and so on.

There is some impact in those areas too. For example, my interpersonal relationships aren’t very good, and I’m always on my own. Emotionally, I also don’t really dare to express my thoughts, because I’m afraid of being rejected or not understood.
Mm, I understand. In your interactions with professors, do you have similar feelings?
Yes, I’m very afraid to go to professors, to ask questions or communicate. I always feel like the questions I ask are stupid, and that they’ll leave a bad impression on the professor.
It seems that professors hold a very important place in your academic life. How do you understand this fear?
Mm, yes. I always feel that professors are the people who judge my ability, and their evaluations are very important, so I’m even more afraid of making mistakes.
You place a lot of importance on your professors’ evaluations, is that right?
Yes. Changing the ddl, the deadline, is because I’m worried I won’t do well and I’m afraid of facing failure. So I always want to put it off a bit, and avoid it if I can.
I understand. This fear of failure leads you to choose procrastination. When did this feeling start?
Okay, I’m a little nervous. Talking about these topics feels a bit uncomfortable.
I understand how you feel. Discussing these topics can make people feel uneasy. What kind of impact do you think repeatedly changing the ddl has? I really care about your thoughts.

Mostly self-blame and anxiety. I feel like maybe I’m useless, always dragging things out. I’m also worried that the professor’s opinion of me will get worse, that they’ll think I’m not serious or responsible.
It feels like there’s so much stirring around inside you. That really is a lot to worry about.
Yes, I’m always overthinking these things in my head, and the more I think about them, the more anxious I get.

I can understand your anxiety. Indeed, in a teacher-student relationship, there is inevitably pressure from being assessed or evaluated, and that may have intensified your anxiety. Can you share with me why you decided to change the ddl in the first place?
I think it was because I was worried I wasn’t good enough. I was afraid that if I submitted on time, it wouldn’t meet the standard I had in mind, so I procrastinated.
You’re worried that you won’t be able to complete it according to the standard you expect of yourself, is that right?
Yes, I always have very high expectations for myself and want to do things perfectly, but every time I can’t, I feel very disappointed.
Mm-hmm. I imagine you must have had a lot of considerations at the time, and that’s why you made that choice in the end.
Yes, I always weigh things back and forth, and in the end I still go down the old path of procrastination.
I hear your distress.
Sometimes I also feel like I’m pretty stupid. I clearly know procrastination isn’t good, but I still can’t change this problem.
You feel helpless about yourself, don’t you?
Yes, I also feel very conflicted. I want to do well, but I’m afraid I won’t do well, and in the end I get awkwardly stuck in the middle.
It sounds like you’re struggling between two kinds of emotions.
Yes, I’ve tried making schedules, setting time blocks to do things, and I’ve also tried studying with classmates so we can supervise each other, but these methods only work for a short time.
Those methods only work temporarily, is that right?
I’ve also tried reducing the time I spend on my phone, and giving my phone to someone else to hold onto for a while. Sometimes that helps me focus a little, but it’s not a long-term solution.
You really have made some efforts. Coming here today is already a very important step.
Thank you for saying that. Maybe starting by saying these problems out loud is also a way of facing them.

You mentioned a very important word: facing. It means you’re working hard to become different, and that’s something very hopeful. Thank you for being so brave. As we’ve talked up to this point, what would you hope Xiaotian can help you with?
I hope I can find some more effective ways to deal with procrastination, especially when facing important academic tasks, so I can overcome that fear of failure.
Go ahead.
Also, how to improve my confidence, so I don’t care so much about other people’s opinions and can focus more on my own goals.
Could you say a bit more about what it feels like to care about other people’s opinions?
Yes, I long to be recognized and understood, and I also long to be able to face challenges bravely like other people do.

I understand. At the same time, it seems there are some socially learned boundaries affecting you. Can we break this issue down a bit? When you describe this confusion, there are actually several points with quite a bit of tension. Shall we look at them one by one?
Okay, I think that might make things clearer.

First is the impulse to confide in someone. As you said, behind this there seems to be a desire to be truly understood. This means that right now you feel you haven’t been truly understood. I’m not sure if I’m expressing that accurately.
Yes, I feel like I’m always misunderstood, or that I haven’t been able to clearly express what’s inside me. I hope someone can truly see my effort and confusion.
What is it that still hasn’t been understood? Can you tell me about it?
For example, my seriousness and effort. Sometimes I work very hard to do something, but the result isn’t good, and I always feel like no one sees my effort—they only see the result.
Mm. You really hope to be seen by them. After all, you are so serious about it, and you’ve already been working very hard in how you approach this.
Yes, I always hope people can see my effort, instead of just criticizing that my results aren’t good enough.
Mm-hmm. Worrying that you’re not good enough, worrying about making mistakes.
Every time I face criticism and blame, I always feel very helpless and very small, and I even question my own ability and effort.
I’m thinking that when you face criticism and blame, you feel very powerless and start doubting yourself.
Yes, I am indeed a little afraid of facing the real me, afraid of seeing the side of me that isn’t good enough. This self-doubt and uneasiness make me feel really bad.
Mm, I can feel that this is really very painful for you.
Yes, doing this avoids pain in the short term, but in the long run it’s an even bigger kind of avoidance.

Actually, when we tell others what’s really in our hearts, especially things that are troubling or bothering us, it really can bring up a sense of shame. Because most of us probably aren’t used to doing that. So it can feel very unnatural, and that feeling can feel very unfamiliar. I really understand how you feel, and that makes me feel even more that it’s remarkable that you came here so bravely to talk. It’s full of courage.
Thank you for your understanding and encouragement. I feel a little lighter. Saying what’s in my heart really does take some courage.

Mm-hmm. Then I’d like to talk about the relational side of things. What was your relationship originally like? What kind of relationship might be needed for the behavior you want to achieve? Is it possible that some disclosure from you could help promote the relationship? Relationships are built and maintained gradually by us, so sometimes they can feel complicated and tangled. But that’s very normal.
I understand. I’ll think about these questions. Maybe this will help me understand the direction of my own behavior.
Yes, thinking about these things may help us do an “analysis” of our own behavior. Mm, what major are you studying?
I’m studying computer science.
Good. Have you had any experience with counseling before?
I’m not very familiar with it. This is my first time receiving counseling.
I understand. This is your first counseling experience.
No, this is my first time. I hope that through counseling I can find some ways to resolve my confusion.
Okay. My undergraduate and graduate studies were both in counseling, and I was trained overseas.
That sounds very professional. What you said makes me feel confident.
Thank you. I’ll do my best to help you.
Thank you for your patience and understanding. I feel today’s conversation was very helpful.

You’re welcome, and thank you for your affirmation! I can feel your motivation for self-growth. Since we need to end this session, I will continue to care about your mood and feelings. Today we mainly talked about your procrastination. I saw you analyze and express yourself clearly, and begin to face yourself, which is very important. There may still be many challenges in life, and you’re welcome to come back here to talk again. We’ll stop here for today. Goodbye!
Good afternoon.
Where are you right now?
At home.
Mm-hmm.
I didn’t go to school today.
Can you tell me why you didn’t go to school today?
Yeah, I just didn’t want to go out.
Mm-hmm. What does that feeling of not wanting to go out feel like?
It’s okay, I guess.
Could you tell me in more detail what you’ve been through this week?
I just feel really annoyed.
Mm-hmm. You just said “okay, I guess.” Could you say a bit more specifically?
Mm, sometimes I want to study, and once I start I lose track of time. Then suddenly I don’t want to move and feel irritated.
Mm-hmm. How do your weeks usually go?
It’s pretty much always like this, going in circles.
It sounds like this has been really troubling for you. What kinds of things or emotions usually make you suddenly not want to move?
Sometimes I feel really awful too, and stay in bed all day.
Do you feel awful all the time, or does that feeling only happen at certain times?
Mm-hmm, it’s there.
Okay, let’s keep talking. I’ll summarize what you’ve mentioned so far.
It’s okay.
You messaged earlier that you can even fall asleep during the 10-minute break between classes.
Yes, when I’m tired, I can fall asleep no matter what.
Has there been anything recently that’s made you feel especially tired?
Okay.
I was waiting for your message just now. Have you been feeling more tired lately?
Yes, I always feel exhausted.
Mm-hmm.
It feels like every day is draining me.
What time do you usually rest at night? Last time you mentioned you get up at seven in the morning.
Recently it’s been pretty late, after 11.
Mm-hmm, so what time do you go to sleep at night?
Right, usually after 11.
Mm, that is a bit late. What do you usually do before bed?
My phone, studying, reading, sometimes just zoning out and doing nothing.
Do these activities affect your ability to fall asleep?
Yes, I’ve been sleeping restlessly all along.
What do you feel is causing you to sleep restlessly?
I wake up very easily.
How long has this been going on?
It’s very boring, repetitive.
Mm, I understand.
Really, every day feels like I’m living the same day over and over.
Mm-hmm, that kind of life does sound dull and repetitive. What kind of life would feel not dull and not repetitive to you?
I don’t know, maybe if something new happened.
Would you want there to be some changes in your life?
I’m not sure. Sometimes I also feel like this is pretty safe.
Mm, I understand. Sometimes we tend to keep things the way they are because it gives us a sense of safety.
Right, it’s kind of conflicted.
Mm, so this kind of life feels a bit contradictory for you. On one hand it feels safe, and on the other hand it feels dull and repetitive.
Sometimes I think it’s pretty good, at least there aren’t any big ups and downs.
Mm-hmm. When you say it’s pretty good, what do you mean?
Because this way I feel calmer inside, without too many ups and downs.
That feeling of calm is important to you, right?
Other things are the things that make me irritated or upset.
Mm, these things that make you irritated or upset—what kinds of things are they usually?
Thinking about the times I was bullied, and things at home.
It sounds like these things have a big impact on you. Could you share something recently that made you especially unhappy?
Yesterday, my parents argued again.
I see. That kind of thing really can be very upsetting. Can you say how it affects you?
Things from when I was little. I don’t want to talk about it.
Mm-hmm, I remember you told me about that.
Mm.
Mm, I can understand you. You just mentioned that your current repetitive, dull life means unhappy things won’t happen. Could we talk about what you think of this kind of life?
Unhappy things still happen. I just want to shut myself away to avoid more sad things.
Oh, I understand. So shutting yourself away is to avoid more unhappiness.
Because once there’s change, something bad might happen.
You mean changes in life often make you feel uneasy, right?
It’s like there’s a breath of air stuck in my chest, and I can’t let it out.
It sounds like that feeling is really painful. When do you especially feel this irritability?
When things don’t go my way, or when I suddenly think of things from the past.
Mm-hmm. What do you do when you feel irritated?
Sleep, or zone out.
I understand. Sleeping and zoning out can indeed help ease the emotions for a while.
A little better, but the problem still isn’t solved.
Mm-hmm. It seems like you feel these methods don’t solve the root problem, right?
But it’s no use. Sometimes I get so annoyed I don’t even want to live.
It hurts to hear you say that. That feeling must be extremely painful. Can you tell me what makes you feel there’s no meaning in living?
I feel like there’s no meaning in living. Everything is so boring.
I hear you saying that life feels very boring. In fact, you’re expressing the confusion and irritability inside you. Would you be willing to talk about when these feelings started?
Yes, I want to know what exactly is going on with me.
How often does irritability show up in your life, and how intense is it, if 100 means the strongest level?
The frequency isn’t very high, but once it appears, it’s very strong, probably around 70 or 80.
For example, how many times a week, and how long does it last each time?
Two or three times a week, a few hours each time, sometimes even a whole day.
I see. How long does this state usually last?
At the longest, I’ve been unable to pull myself together for two or three weeks in a row.
Then each time this emotion appears, what do you usually do to cope with it?
At least an hour, I guess. Sometimes it lasts the whole day.
Do you choose to sleep to escape this irritated feeling? And how intense is the irritability you usually feel, from 1 to 100?
85. Very strong.
Mm, I hear how you feel. Very intense irritability.
Right.
Actually, irritability is a very normal emotion. Everyone can have it.
But I feel like I can’t control myself.
I understand how you feel. We can try some ways to cope with this emotion.
A name? Like “dark cloud”?
Irritability is like a little troublemaker separate from us. It shows up from time to time and makes us feel uncomfortable.
Mm, I understand.
Next time, if this emotion appears again, you can try stopping and observing it, and see what is happening at that moment. Try spending some time with this little troublemaker. See what happens.
Okay, I’ll try.
Mm-hmm. Our time is up for today, and our counseling process will be coming to an end very soon.
Oh, really?
I’m very glad that during this time, I’ve heard you share so many things with me.
Mm-hmm, thank you for listening to me.
How have these chats felt for you? I’d like to hear your real feelings.
Really good. It feels like I found someone I can talk to honestly, like a close confidant.
Hearing you use the word “confidant” makes me feel very warm.
You really helped me a lot.
Thank you so much for your trust as well, which allowed us to walk through this journey together.
Being able to chat with you has made me feel much better.
I’m very glad to hear you say that. Can you tell me what helped you feel a little better? I look forward to hearing your story again next time.
Lately my sleep problems have been really bothering me. It feels like every night there’s some kind of thought controlling me, telling me not to fall asleep.
I understand. Could you tell me a bit more specifically?

Actually, I just came back to school not long ago, and I was thinking I’d slowly start getting used to the school schedule again. At home I usually go to sleep at 10:30, but at school I have to wait until my roommates turn off the lights, which is 12. Before, my schedule at school was pretty normal. Once the lights went off at 12, I could usually fall asleep, and then get up at 7 in the morning. But these past few days, I don’t know why, every few days I can’t sleep the whole night. The more I can’t sleep, the more anxious I get, and the more anxious I get, the less I can sleep. Every day I basically don’t get into deep sleep until around 4. I really don’t know what to do.
How long has this been going on?
It’s probably been going on for a little over a week. I really don’t know how to fix it.
I understand. Would it be okay to tell me some basic information about yourself? For example, your gender, age, and whether you’re a student or working?
Okay. I’m female, 21 years old this year, and I’m a college student.
Okay. Are you an undergraduate or a graduate student?
Um, not graduate. I’m an undergraduate, in my junior year.
Okay.

I also think it’s really strange. My sleep schedule at school never had any problems before, but after coming back this time, I started having insomnia frequently. A few days ago, one of my roommates, who’s a night owl, said to me, “You fall asleep so early. The lights had only been off for half an hour, and I already heard you snoring.” At the time I didn’t know what she meant by saying that, but I felt like maybe my falling asleep early was affecting them, or maybe she was making fun of me for sleeping like an old person. After hearing those words, I really took it to heart, and I don’t know if that also affected my sleep.

Mm-hmm. You said it’s been going on for over a week now, that you go to sleep very late at night, it’s hard to fall asleep, and your sleep quality isn’t good. You can only sleep really soundly when you’re very tired.
Yes, my situation really is getting worse and worse. Even my mental state during daytime classes is really poor. Do I need to see a doctor?
Have you tried any methods before to help you fall asleep, like melatonin or things like that?
The time I actually fall asleep is probably around 4 a.m. I can only finally fall asleep when I’m very, very tired.
Mm, that must be really troubling for you. Around what time do you get into bed to sleep?

It should be that after the lights go off at 12, I can slowly enter a sleep state, like before, when I could fall asleep within half an hour. I also know sleeping at 12 might be a little late, but it’s much better than 4 a.m.
Mm, I understand how you feel. You mentioned that your sleep problems now have a big impact on how you feel during the day, and that is indeed quite concerning.
Yes, I just feel like every time I lie in bed, my mind can’t stop. It seems like I’m being controlled by some kind of thought that won’t let me fall asleep.
Do you feel like there are certain specific thoughts that keep you from sleeping? And when exactly do you usually start lying in bed and getting ready to fall asleep?
Usually at 11:30. I get into bed half an hour early to get ready to enter a sleep state.
I see.
Okay, thank you.
You’re welcome.
Actually, I also know that sometimes it might be an issue with my mindset. I slept really well at home before, and I didn’t expect that once I came back to school, I’d start having insomnia.

I see. Using your phone before bed can indeed affect sleep. Blue light can make people more alert and affect sleep. You just mentioned, “If there’s that thing, proactive and retroactive effects, then I won’t look at it.” Could you tell me what you mean by that?

Mm, I know blue light can affect falling asleep, but sometimes I really can’t help it and scroll for a bit. By proactive and retroactive effects, I mean the phone might interfere with sleep. If these things really do have an effect, then I’ll try not to look at my phone.
I understand. So you’re also aware that looking at your phone may affect your ability to fall asleep. Have you tried not using your phone before bed to see whether it makes it easier to fall asleep?
I haven’t tried completely not looking at my phone yet, but I want to try next. I also know this might be a reason, but I always feel like my phone helps me relax a little.
That’s understandable. Many people have similar feelings. If you don’t look at your phone, what other ways do you think could help you relax?
Yes, you could say that. Actually, besides my phone, before I go to sleep I also think about all kinds of school-related things, like studying, tasks assigned by teachers, future plans, and so on.
Mm-hmm. When you say your sleep quality isn’t good, what do you mean by that?

It’s like I feel I’m in light sleep the whole night. I’m easily woken up by sounds around me, and after I fall asleep, I also dream about a lot of strange things. When I wake up, my body doesn’t feel well recovered, and my mental state the next day is very poor.
Mm-hmm. When you say your state isn’t good, what do you mean? For example, is it feeling groggy, or something else?
It’s that my brain is still awake, but my arms and legs are especially tired, and my eyes feel sore and uncomfortable, like I haven’t fully woken up.
Mm-hmm, I see. So your brain is still awake, and your eyes feel uncomfortable.
Yes, that’s exactly the feeling. Every day when I get up, I feel especially exhausted, as if I hadn’t slept at all.

I understand. The phone use before bed and thinking about all kinds of things that you mentioned really may affect your ability to fall asleep and your sleep quality. You said you think a lot when you’re sleeping. Is it before falling asleep that you think a lot? What specific things do you think about?

Before falling asleep, I keep thinking about things, like what I need to do the next day, academic pressure, future career planning, and so on. In short, all kinds of things keep repeating in my mind, making it very hard for me to calm down.
Mm, I understand. Let’s look together at how we can help you sort through these thoughts and find some ways to cope with them, okay?
Actually, after talking, I feel a bit better. At least now I know some possible reasons, and I have some directions for improving things. I hope I can slowly adjust back.
Mm-hmm, that’s great.
Thank you sincerely for your help. I’ll try not looking at my phone and relaxing myself before bed. I hope I can slowly get back to normal.
You’re very welcome.
Thank you. Goodbye.
Mm-hmm. I wish you all the best. Goodbye.
Hello, I’d like to talk with you.
Hello, I’m Xiaotian, a counselor. What would you like to talk about today?
My relationship with my boyfriend has been really troubling me lately. I really like him, but sometimes I can’t stand his temper, and I don’t know what to do.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happened?

I feel like I have a pretty good temper, and I rarely have conflicts with other people. But my boyfriend is the kind of person who doesn’t like arguing, and every time he tries hard to hold himself back. Have you had any thoughts or plans about this kind of married life?
I’ve thought about divorce, but then I feel it would be too hasty, especially since there’s the baby.
I’d really like to know your thoughts in more detail.
Sometimes I feel that if my husband could change and think more about me, maybe our relationship would get better.
You’ve always been working very hard to hold up your own life. You’re an independent person.
Yes, but sometimes I also hope someone can share the burden. I don’t want all the pressure to be on me alone.
It sounds like you really do need more support and someone to share the burden with you.
Especially when I think about the future, I feel afraid of living like this.
Life in the future feels full of challenges and uncertainty for you.
Yes, when we got married, his family had a lot of demands. It feels like I’ve been meeting their needs the whole time, and no one ever considered my feelings.
It sounds like you’ve been under a lot of pressure in this relationship. Have you talked to him about these feelings you’ve been carrying?
I’ve talked to my husband many times, hoping he could think more about me.
How did he respond at the time?
He always says he’ll change, but in terms of actual action, I haven’t seen any change.
When you hear him respond like that, what goes through your mind?
Yes, it feels like I’m talking to a wall, like I’m not being valued at all.
After he responds that way, how do you usually deal with it?
Sometimes I lose my temper too, but it seems like that only makes us argue more.
After you lose your temper, you two argue. More specifically, what does that interaction look like?
Yes, a lot of the time I don’t even want to say anything anymore. I feel like there’s no point.
What about him himself? It sounds like you also have a lot of disappointment and sadness toward him. Have you two talked about that part?
We talked about it at the beginning, but later he would always avoid it, or say he didn’t know what to do.
Mm, it sounds like he may feel a bit at a loss and doesn’t know how to respond.
Yes, he’s willing to listen, but actually doing it is especially hard for him.
That makes you feel like his change hasn’t made any real progress, right?
Sometimes I feel like he doesn’t really want to change at all, that he’s just saying it.
You feel he hasn’t truly invested himself in the process of changing. How do you usually tell him how you feel?
I tell him my feelings directly. I say I need his support and understanding, not just verbal promises.
Mm, I can feel that you’re very invested in this relationship. Earlier you mentioned sometimes feeling like an outsider. Could you say more about that part?
Yes, that’s exactly the feeling. He always speaks up for his mother and ignores my feelings.
That would feel very hurtful, because the person living life with you is your husband.
Yes. My husband doesn’t stand on my side, and I feel especially lonely and helpless.
It sounds like this loneliness and helplessness are really painful for you. Can you say more about what that feels like?
I’m very disappointed. I feel like he has no sense of responsibility and isn’t mature.
Hearing you say that, you’re very disappointed in his behavior, and you feel he isn’t mature enough or responsible enough.
Yes, mainly because my mother-in-law really wants a grandson.
Your mother-in-law’s expectations have put quite a lot of pressure on you, right?
Actually, I also want a child, but I want it to be a shared wish between the two of us.
I understand. You want this to be a decision you and your husband make together, not just because of the expectations of the elders.
Yes, having a baby is my biggest hope and motivation.
On the other hand, I also seem to hear some worries.
Yes, I’m especially worried that my mother-in-law will interfere too much in the child’s education.
Right, it sounds like this also affects your emotions.
Yes, sometimes when I think about the future, my heart feels very heavy.
For example, what kinds of things? Could you give me an example?
For example, my mother-in-law is always hinting that she hopes I’ll have a boy, and that puts a lot of pressure on me.
Oh, so she doesn’t say it outright, but she gives you the feeling that she’s expecting it to be a boy.
Yes, every time she mentions it like it’s unintentional, but I know she truly hopes I’ll have a boy.
It sounds like these seemingly unintentional hints make you feel a lot of pressure. Do you often think about these issues?
Yes, I’d rather it be a girl.
I hear you bringing up the gender you’re hoping for. Does your husband feel the same way as you?
Yes, and this is another point of conflict between us.
I can sense that the difference between you on this issue has brought some distress. What is the living situation like right now?
Not yet, but my husband insists that his mother move in with us.

That really is a topic that can feel stressful. What I’d like to understand more is, when you’re facing these family pressures and conflicts, how do you usually regulate your emotions or find some ways to ease them?
I try to keep myself busy and not think about these upsetting things. Sometimes I also talk with friends.

Mm, that kind of approach can indeed help distract you a bit. When you mention your mother-in-law, I notice you have some views about her. Can you tell me specifically what you dislike most about her?
Yes, I feel like she says all the right things on the surface, but what she actually does doesn’t match at all.
It sounds like you feel very confused and dissatisfied with this behavior of hers. In situations like this, do you choose to give yourself some time alone, to sort through your thoughts?
Yes, sometimes I don’t want to deal with her, so I just stay in the bedroom.
Do you feel that getting along with her is relatively difficult?
Exactly. I don’t like hypocritical people. I always feel that people who say one thing and mean another are hard to get along with.
It seems you appreciate people whose words and actions match, right?
Yes, especially when I think about having to live with my mother-in-law long-term in the future, I get even more worried.
When you think about the future, there are a lot of worries and concerns in your heart.
Yes, especially when I think about having to live with my mother-in-law long-term in the future, I get even more worried.
When you think about the days ahead, there are a lot of emotions, like anger, feeling wronged, and worry. How do you usually deal with these emotions?
I usually cry. After crying it out, I feel a little better.
Crying can also be a way of releasing emotions.
Yes, crying it out makes me feel a bit lighter.
When you feel sad, besides crying, are there other ways you express your emotions?
Yes, we’re far apart, and I don’t want my mom to worry.
Mm-hmm.
Sometimes I also write in a diary, writing out how I’m feeling.
How often can you usually go home? It sounds like you really are quite far from your hometown.
Usually only once every six months. It’s pretty far.
That really is quite a long time. Does writing in a diary help you sort through your emotions?
It helps a bit, but before long I start feeling sad again.
Mm-hmm, it feels like this method sometimes can’t fully ease your emotions either.
Sometimes I really feel very helpless.
It sounds really hard. What kind of support do you feel you need most?
Yes, I feel like I’m facing too many problems, and I feel especially powerless.
Have these feelings affected other areas of your daily life, like eating and sleeping? Are those affected?
Yes, sometimes I don’t sleep well. I’m awake the whole night.
In terms of sleep, is it easy for you to fall asleep?
No, it’s not easy. After I lie down, my mind is full of all kinds of messy things, and no matter what, I can’t fall asleep.
Mm, it sounds like there’s a feeling of it always working against you, leaving you feeling helpless.
Yes, the more I think, the less I can sleep, and it’s really depressing.
That sounds really distressing. Besides your sleep being affected, are there any other areas where you feel powerless or depressed?
Sometimes I don’t have much appetite when I eat either. I feel like I don’t want to eat anything.
Your eating has been affected too. When you usually eat less, do you notice any particular physical reactions?
Yes. Sometimes I feel completely drained and don’t want to do anything.

I understand. Mm, I noticed you mentioned that your emotions have been affected by your husband’s family, and that you feel angry and hurt. What do you feel are the main things that make you feel this way?
Okay, thank you.

You’ve shared a lot with me today about your emotions during pregnancy and how you’ve been affected by your husband’s family. I’d like to know, among all these feelings, what is troubling you the most?

A little better. I feel like I’ve been heard a bit.

I’m glad to be able to explore these issues with you. At this stage, we have real people assisting the AI behind the scenes. Was there any feeling from this conversation that felt especially important to you?
