I really want to be able to get out of these feelings, because I know that if this keeps going, it will only be painful for me. I know this person isn’t right for me, but I just can’t control my feelings.
I understand. Can you say more about what feels especially painful for you?

Every time I have work-related interactions with him, I get really nervous, even a bit flustered. Then afterward, I keep replaying those interactions over and over, feeling like I did terribly, and I’m full of regret.
It sounds like you feel very dissatisfied with how you acted in those interactions, and that must feel really hard for you.
Mm, I know. Actually, I feel like these feelings make me very uncomfortable. On one hand, I hope I can be close to him, but on the other hand, I clearly know that this isn’t good for me.
Struggling with such conflicting feelings can really be exhausting. Could you say a bit more about how that feels for you?
I’m always swinging back and forth in this conflict, and I feel really tired inside.
What kind of feeling does this back-and-forth bring up for you?
Sometimes I feel at a loss, and I don’t even know how to face him.
What is that feeling of being at a loss like, specifically?
Yes, and at the same time it feels very complicated, because there is liking him in my heart, but also a lot of confusion and anxiety.
It sounds like you’re facing emotions that are very complicated and conflicted?
Mm-hmm. It really is a very painful feeling. There’s a lot of guilt, liking, confusion, and struggling, right?
You’ve been going through a lot of emotional pain and struggle.
Yes, it’s like being in a whirlpool, not knowing how to break free.
I can understand that you feel trapped in this emotional whirlpool, like there’s no way out.
What I mean by wanting to get out is that I want to be completely freed from these feelings, and no longer be troubled by these unrealistic feelings.
You want to find a way to truly get free from these troubling and painful feelings, right?
Yes. On one hand, I want to have contact with him, but on the other hand, I also know that nothing will come of it.
I understand the struggle inside you. One part of you hopes to keep in touch, while another part of you realizes this path may not work out.
I feel like maybe I should give all of this up and stop being caught up in him.
It sounds like this relationship is causing you a lot of pain.
I want to end this hopeless crush, completely let go of my feelings for him, and no longer be affected by him.
You long to get out of the current situation and return to a state of inner calm.
Yes, I feel like only then might I be able to regain calm and refocus on my own life.
That’s the goal you’re hoping for, right?

Mm-hmm. But at the beginning, you said what made you feel bad was the way he was inconsistent with you? Yes, some of his behaviors would make me feel like there was a little hope, but soon after he would make me completely disappointed again. This back and forth is really painful for me.
His behavior has made you go through a repeated cycle of hope and disappointment.
Yes, every time there’s new hope, and then it quickly gets shattered. It feels like my heart is being tortured over and over.
This repetition has brought you a great deal of emotional distress.
Yes.
This makes me think that you may be feeling deeply hurt and unsettled. I wonder, besides these, are there any other feelings?
Yes, there are. Sometimes I feel like he doesn’t really care about my feelings, and he’s just handling the relationship with me from his own perspective.
Yes. Can you say more about what makes you angry?
I feel like sometimes he acts as if he has feelings for me, but later he seems very distant again. I feel like I’ve been played.
You feel like he’s always coming from his own perspective.
Yes, like he only considers his own needs and doesn’t take my feelings into account.
That leaves you stuck in this very confused place.
Yes, it makes me very confused, and I don’t know how I should face him.
That sounds really painful. Can you describe what the feeling is like within this confusion?
Yes, that’s exactly the feeling. So I’ve decided I should completely let go and protect myself.
Letting go of him takes a great deal of courage for you. Can you share more about the process of deciding to let go?
Yes, I feel really wronged and very sad, but I really am powerless to change his attitude.
Do you usually have any ways to express your anger?
I haven’t found any suitable way yet. Most of the time, I can only silently bear it on my own.
You said you feel dizzy. Do you feel discomfort in any other parts of your body?
Yes, sometimes I feel dizzy and weak. It may be related to psychological stress.
Can you describe this dizziness and weakness more specifically?
It’s like my head feels very heavy, and sometimes my vision even goes dark, and I just have no energy at all.
Mm, then we can try some relaxation methods. Now gently place your hand on your head and slowly touch it. What do you notice?
I feel a little better now. Maybe because I’ve talked about it, I feel a bit lighter emotionally.
If you’re willing, you can try taking a long, deep breath. As you exhale, you can make an “aaaa” sound, or let out a sigh. I’ll be here to support you.
Okay, I’ll try taking a deep breath. I do feel a bit better, thank you.
Good. The deep breathing seems to be working well. Please keep staying relaxed. How do you feel?
I'm here.
Vanora, I was just waiting for you.
Mm, I was also waiting to talk with you about what's been going on with me.
Mm-hmm, it's okay, and I'm sorry to have kept you waiting.
It's okay. Lately I’ve really been feeling so powerless, and I need someone to listen to me.
You can tell me more.
I don’t know where to start, but I really want you to understand the situation I’m in right now.
Mm-hmm, how would you put it?
My family situation is very complicated. I grew up in a blended family.
I understand. That kind of family situation can definitely bring up some complicated feelings. Can you tell me more about your situation?
Yes. I feel like my mom is pushing me so hard I can’t even breathe.
What has she done to you that makes you feel this way?
She hits me, almost every day, and she scolds me over everything.
Mm, I know this must be really painful for you. Can we talk a bit more about what exactly happened?
Every time she hits me, she hits me while cursing at me, saying I’m useless, saying I’m a vicious dog, a curse.
It sounds like you’ve been through a lot. When she says those things each time, it must hurt a lot, right?
Yeah. Every time she says those things, I feel like I really am terrible, like I’m worthless.
Mm, I understand how you feel. Would you be willing to share more with me about what it was like at the time? If you don’t feel like talking about it for now, we can also leave it for now.
I can talk about it. I don’t want these things to keep troubling me.
You’re right. These experiences really do need to be worked through. We can take our time and talk about what’s been going on between you and your mom.
Maybe she’s biased against me. She thinks I’m a burden from her ex-husband, so she’s been tormenting me all along.
I can understand why you would think that. Can you say a little more about how she torments you?
Yes. Every time I seem to be in a bad mood, she hits me even more violently, scolds me, and makes me feel like I can’t breathe.
That must make you feel extremely painful. Has she ever said why she treats you this way?
She says I affect the family atmosphere, and that I don’t deserve to stay in this home.
It sounds like she takes a lot of her negative emotions out on you. You feel very helpless, right?
She has never been my friend. She’s always treated me like an outsider, or like a bad influence.
So, has her attitude toward you never changed?
Yeah. I don’t know why she’s always so unfriendly to me.
I hear that you’re trying hard to understand her behavior, and that really is painful. So, how would you like us to face these feelings next?
Yes, she isn’t even a friend. Why does she treat me this way? Those letters and words really make me fall apart.
Mm-hmm. It added so much pain to you for no reason, and she completely doesn’t understand the hurt she caused, so you really would feel angry and wronged.
Yes, I’m really angry, and I feel especially wronged. Why do I have to bear all of this?
And because you’re dealing with depression, it can also be easier for you to believe other people’s negative judgments of you. It really makes things even worse.
Yes. I feel like I’m really worthless. Every day I question whether my existence is a mistake.
I understand, and I understand your anger and how wronged you feel. And also that feeling of really wanting to drag her over and make her apologize.
Yes. I really hope she can realize the harm she’s caused me and come apologize to me.

She doesn’t know how much harm that one action of hers caused you; she only knows that her own mood was affected. You hope she’ll apologize, so at least you might feel a bit better and not so easily believe the things she said.
Yes. If she could apologize, maybe I wouldn’t so easily believe those insulting things she said about me.
Mm-hmm. Carrying this hurt for so many years has really not been easy.
It’s really hard. I feel like I almost can’t keep going.
I can feel how hard things are for you right now. This feeling must be very painful for you.
Really? I really want to learn how to let go, but it’s really hard.
Letting go really isn’t easy, especially after going through so much.
Today she hit me again, just because I didn’t wash the bowls clean enough. She also scolded me and said I’m worthless.
It sounds like what happened today was really unfair and painful for you.
Yes. When I think of those excessive things she said and her violence, my heart hurts in waves.
I understand. These experiences really can make someone feel very painful and angry.
Yes. I feel like these things have been weighing on my heart, making it hard for me to breathe.
When these feelings build up inside, it really can feel very painful. Finding a way to express or release these emotions may help you.
I’m willing to, but I’m also a little worried about whether it will work.
I can understand your worry. Can you tell me more about how you’re feeling?
Mm, I understand that my emotions need to be released, but I don’t really know exactly what to do.
I’m really glad you’re willing to try releasing your emotions. Maybe we can explore some methods together and see what helps you the most.
Okay, I’m willing to try. Every time I think of her, I feel angry, and I need to find an outlet.
Okay, then we can try some methods. For example, you could try hitting a stuffed doll to express your emotions, or write down your feelings and tear up the pieces of paper. How does that sound?
I think hitting a stuffed doll suits me better. I can also say to her the things I’ve always wanted to say.
That sounds like a good idea. Do you have any stuffed dolls at home?
Yes, I have a few stuffed dolls I can use.
Great. Then shall we try this for this week? When you feel angry, you can use this method, and next time we can talk about how you felt.
Okay, I’ll try it.
You can also say the things you want to say to her while you’re hitting the stuffed doll.
Okay. I’ll try saying my anger and hurt out loud to the stuffed doll.
Mm-hmm, okay. Our counseling time for this session is almost up. Is there anything else you’d like to tell me?
Not for now. I feel a little lighter. Thank you for listening to me.
Mm-hmm. I’m really glad to hear that you feel a little lighter. Do you still remember the methods we discussed? I hope you can keep using them to take good care of yourself, okay?
Mm, I’ll try hard not to hurt myself. I’ll try other ways.
That’s great. Then shall we still meet next Monday evening?
Yes, next Monday works. See you then.
Remember to book the appointment, so you’ll get a reminder. If you’re willing, you can also fill out the feedback form to help us improve. Bye-bye.
Hello, teacher.
What would you like to talk with me about today?
Lately I’ve been thinking about whether to buy an iPad, but I feel really torn and don’t know if I should buy it.
It sounds like you feel a bit conflicted about this. Would you be willing to say more about what you’re thinking?
Mm, it is pretty nice, but I always feel like I don’t deserve to have something that expensive.
It sounds like you’re having some self-doubt, as if you feel you may not be worthy of having something like that?
Yeah. I’ve always been very frugal, and I feel like my family’s financial situation is just average, so buying something expensive feels a bit extravagant.
I can understand your frugality, especially when there’s a lot of financial pressure at home. That feeling can become even stronger.
Mm, I’m still a student now, and my family’s financial pressure isn’t small either. Maybe this money would be more useful if it were spent somewhere else.
You’re considering this from many angles. In this situation, how to use money really is something that needs careful thought. Do you have any other worries?
Yes. I always feel like I’m not good enough right now, that I don’t deserve nice things, and that I have to work harder first.
Why does Lulu feel she’s being underestimated? Is it related to salary?
Mm, on one hand it’s about money, and on the other hand it’s that I feel I’m not that outstanding, so I can’t afford to use such nice things.

It seems this involves the difference between your family’s perspective and your own perspective and thoughts. Your parents care about age, and that makes them overlook Lulu’s other strengths. I get the sense that Lulu knows she has many strengths and feels she deserves a very good partner to share life with.
Yeah. My parents are pretty frugal, and I’ve been influenced by them since I was little. I always feel like I don’t deserve those good things.
Mm-hmm. When they say that, it makes you feel uncomfortable because it makes you feel underestimated?
Yes. I think what they say isn’t completely wrong, but sometimes I also feel like I’m being underestimated a bit.
Deep down, does Lulu sometimes feel that your current boyfriend hasn’t fully met your expectations?
Yeah, sometimes I do feel that way, but then I also wonder if my standards are too high.
Comparisons in relationships are very natural, but everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses in different areas, like salary, ability, being family-oriented, taking care of others, and so on.
Mm, I know everyone has strengths and weaknesses, but I still feel a bit unbalanced inside.
Does Lulu feel that your boyfriend spends money on you because he feels he’s somewhat not good enough for you?
Sometimes I do think that, like he’s trying to make up for something, but I don’t want him to do that.
What kind of feelings does it bring up for you when your boyfriend does this?
It makes me feel a bit disrespected, as if he thinks I can only accept these things.
Then what does Lulu think is the reason your boyfriend spends money on you? Is he trying to make up for something, or trying to make you happy, or is it something else?
I think maybe he wants to make me happy, and maybe he also feels this can keep me with him.
When your boyfriend says you’re silly, can you say a bit more about what he specifically means?
He thinks I don’t ask much materially, that I’m easily satisfied, and he thinks I’m a bit naive.
When you hear those words, what does Lulu feel? Do you feel a little disappointed or that it’s unfair?
Yes, I do feel that way. I feel like I give too much, but what I get back isn’t proportional.
Mm-hmm, that’s understandable. In your past romantic experiences, has Lulu had similar feelings?
Sometimes I’ve felt that the emotion and time I put in didn’t receive a corresponding return.
Okay. Then what kinds of gifts have you received, or what kinds of care have you experienced, that made you feel happy and satisfied?
Maybe things that are more thoughtful or meaningful. They don’t necessarily have to be expensive, but they need to feel sincere.
Mm. Why do those things make you feel sincerity and care?
Because I feel that caring and thoughtfulness matter more than simply measuring things by money.
I see. Then if, in a relationship, the other person rarely expresses this kind of care and thoughtfulness, how would Lulu feel?
It would make me feel like the other person doesn’t care about me enough, and that the emotional interaction is missing too.
If the Lulu you are now went back to that time, how would you face that person?
I might communicate with him directly and let him know my feelings and expectations.
What kind of feelings do you think it would bring you if the other person had better conditions?
It would mean he has more resources and ability to take my feelings and needs into account, and could give me more of a sense of security.
I see. Then how do you think these resources and abilities affect you in your relationship?
Yes, I also feel very conflicted myself. On one hand, I feel I’m not good enough; on the other hand, I feel I deserve better things.
It sounds like sometimes you may feel you’re not good enough, while at the same time you also sense that you actually deserve better. What is that conflict like for you?
Yes. I’ve always had this fear, that I’ll just stay where I am and not have better development.

It sounds like you have very strong hopes for the future, and also some anxiety, worrying that you’ll stagnate. So regarding the development you want for yourself, do you have any specific expectations?
Mm, yes. I feel like only in that way can I prove that I’m valuable and that I’m worthy of these things.
So you hope to make progress in these areas in order to prove your own value—is that right?
Yes.
These expectations are very important to you. So at this stage, what kinds of steps or support do you think could help you move closer to these goals?
Yes, I’m also trying hard now to think about what I truly need and want.
These pulls in different directions are confusing. Maybe you can think about what kind of relationship Lulu needs? And what kind of work you need?
I hope to have a partner who understands and supports me. In terms of work, I hope there can be room for growth, and that it can reflect my value and abilities.
When you feel the other person doesn’t understand you, what thoughts or feelings do you usually have?
I’ll wonder if I’m being too demanding, but I also feel that I really do have higher pursuits and expectations.
Mm. It sounds like you have very deep expectations and a sense of unwillingness to settle. Can you say more about what these expectations and that unwillingness are like specifically?
It’s like this: I really do care about money, because I feel money represents a kind of recognition and value.

Money does seem to be very important to you. It may represent recognition and value, and that’s very worth exploring. When you receive gifts from your boyfriend, is it a kind of mixed feeling? Happy, but at the same time it brings up some conflicted emotions?
Yes, teacher. I really do feel this conflict, and I’m confused about why I’m like this.

This is very normal and understandable. We can have this kind of conflicted feeling. Maybe you can try thinking about what money means in your life, including its impact on your work and relationship. Our counseling time is coming to an end again. Actually, there’s something that’s been bothering me for a long time. I don’t dare to ask for things easily because I’m afraid of being rejected. It feels like every time I’m rejected, it’s like my heart gets stabbed, worse than any other kind of hurt.
How would you describe that?
In the past, I’ve been hurt many times by blunt rejections. For example, when I asked someone for a small favor or wanted to become friends with someone, I was rejected in a really embarrassing way.
Hearing about these experiences, I can sense how painful and helpless you felt at the time.
Yes, but for me, being rejected feels like my worth has been judged. It’s really painful. I don’t even dare to try or ask anymore, because I’m afraid of being hurt like that again.
What is that fear like?

It’s a kind of tension inside, like I can already foresee the hurt. I think of many times when I asked people questions and got rejected, or scenes where I saw other people being rejected. Those memories are just too painful.
That kind of experience really can be very painful. Could you describe that feeling of fear a bit more specifically?
It’s not only when breaking up that I feel this way. As long as I’m rejected, I feel like I’m not being accepted, and even that my existence is unnecessary. That feeling is really painful.
Mm-hmm. Can you say more specifically how this feeling affects you?

It’s probably that kind of expectation I have for relationships. Every time I think I have some foundation with the other person, I feel like that could become a kind of support. But every time I’m bluntly rejected, it makes me feel like I was wrong.
I understand. That feeling of being rejected hurts you a lot, right?
Actually, in all kinds of relationships, I feel like I should try my best to maintain them, and I’m afraid that making requests or expressing needs will damage the relationship.
This fear keeps you from expressing your needs, is that right?

If I’m this afraid of being rejected and don’t dare to bring up my own needs, I’ll keep suppressing myself, even lose myself. Maybe it’s like in the past, when I clearly didn’t want to do certain things but was forced to do them anyway.
When you spent time playing with her, traveling with her, and talking with her on the phone, what was that experience like for you?

It was exhausting. I didn’t have much time of my own. I felt like I was living under someone else’s needs, not in my own life. But every time, I didn’t dare to refuse, because I was worried it would cause the relationship to fall apart.
So you feel you made a lot of sacrifices in this relationship, right?
Sometimes I also felt the other person’s needs were a bit too much, but I was too embarrassed to say it, as if I was afraid that once I said it, they would leave me.
When you were spending time with her, your feelings weren’t good either. Could you say a bit more about that?
Yes. I felt like I couldn’t be myself at all, always accommodating others. Even when I didn’t want to in my heart, I couldn’t say it out loud.
That must make you feel very tired. Are there any other feelings?
Mm, my enthusiasm for life gradually disappeared too. It felt like everything I did was to cater to others, and it was very dull.
It made you feel that life had become dull. When you heard her say that, what kind of feeling did you have?
When I hear stories about rejection, or about rejecting others, I feel a kind of inexplicable pain, as if I’m always going to meet the same fate too.
Mm, I can understand. Does this feeling make you hope even more that, when a relationship ends, you can still be acknowledged?
Yes. I hope to be acknowledged. Even if the relationship ends, I want to hear some positive feedback, rather than complete negation.
Mm, I can understand your expectation. What kind of impact do you think constantly accommodating others has had on you?
It makes me believe even more that my own feelings are wrong, that I’m not important, and that I’m not worth affirming. Then I become even more afraid to bring up my needs or express myself.
Mm-hmm, I understand.
Thank you for understanding. Actually, I don’t know if I can solve this problem, but I really hope I can change the current situation and stop being so afraid of rejection.
I can understand how you feel. If her previous words and actions made you feel she wasn’t sincere, what emotions would you have?
Then I might doubt people’s sincerity even more, and feel that everyone who gets close to me has some purpose, and isn’t genuinely interacting with me.
It sounds like you may have been through some things that made you feel deceived. Would you be willing to share those experiences?
Mm, I’ve had similar experiences before. It’s happened more than once, and it has made me trust relationships between people less and less.
I understand. Those experiences do sound really painful. Can you tell me how you responded the last time she asked you to go out? And about how many times have you encountered similar situations?

I would still agree, even though inside I was very resistant. Before this, there were probably five or six people, and every time I went through a similar feeling. In the end, the relationship became very stiff.
I can sense the struggle you have when facing these situations. Up to now, what do you think has led you to still choose to trust others, even after going through these things?
Maybe I still long for relationships. I don’t want to believe everyone will be like that. I always feel maybe this time will be different.
The real you?
The real me actually hopes to have a healthy relationship, where I don’t have to accommodate too much, don’t have to be too tense, and can get along honestly.
What led you to make that choice in that situation?
Maybe I was afraid that rejecting others would make me seem not friendly enough, or not sociable enough. This fear of losing the relationship pushed me to make a lot of choices against my own wishes.
What are your thoughts on short-term romantic relationships?
Short-term romance gives people a sense of certainty. You don’t have to invest too much emotion, so you won’t get hurt as easily. For me, it’s a way of protecting myself.
When you chose to enter this relationship at the time, what expectations did you have? What did you hope to get from it?
I hoped to get some emotional comfort from it, to temporarily relax and make myself feel less lonely, even though I knew the relationship wouldn’t last long.
What do you feel the emotional experience in this relationship was like?
Yes, actually I wasn’t especially attracted to her. I just needed somewhere to place my feelings at the time, so I entered the relationship like that.
Let me make sure I understand. You’re saying that from the beginning, you had a sense that this relationship wouldn’t last very long, is that right?
Yes. From the very beginning, I knew this relationship wouldn’t last long, but I still chose to step into it. Maybe it was a kind of helplessness around loneliness.
Does that feeling seem a bit contradictory for you—on one hand, clearly knowing it wouldn’t last, but on the other hand, choosing it because of loneliness?
Yes. I can tell the difference, but sometimes I still chose to compromise. That compromise makes me feel very helpless.
I can understand. You mentioned “hahaha.” What was that about?
“Hahaha” is like laughing at myself. Actually, knowing how to judge people and knowing how to handle this kind of relationship are completely two different things.
Those are indeed two different aspects. So what makes it hard for you to refuse her getting close to you?
Yes, I don’t know how to refuse her getting close. I’m worried that refusing would hurt her, and I’m also afraid of losing the relationship because of it.
I understand. Refusing is something relatively difficult for you, right?
This psychological burden really makes me feel awful. I’m always considering other people’s feelings, but ignoring my own needs.
Could you say a bit more about not knowing how to refuse?
In fact, a lot of the time I don’t have enough confidence to express my true thoughts. I’m always worried that my refusal will bring negative consequences, so I choose to compromise.
It sounds like you have a lot of concerns about rejecting others. Can you talk more specifically about these concerns?

Yes. Sometimes when she makes certain requests, I clearly feel they’re unreasonable, but I don’t dare to refuse directly. I always use various excuses to get through it, like asking her to pay for it herself, and so on.
We can explore some ways of expressing yourself that feel comfortable for you.
Yes, but every time it comes to the key moment, I still can’t fully express my thoughts. I always feel that if I say it out loud, it will trigger emotional reactions from the other person.
Have you tried expressing refusal before?
A few times, but the results were never very good. The other person would either get very angry or become completely cold toward me, which made me really regret it.
Maybe you could try expressing your feelings first, and then explain your needs. Do you think that might make it easier for you to express refusal?
Mm, I haven’t tried that way before. It might indeed be better, but I’m afraid I won’t be able to say it.
Mm-hmm. When she says she’ll go by herself, how do you respond?

I have mixed feelings. On one hand, I feel relieved that I don’t have to go. On the other hand, I feel like she was pushed to that point and had no choice but to go by herself, so I feel a little guilty.
It sounds like when you respond to her, there are many feelings intertwined inside. What do you feel these emotions are showing that you care about?

What I care about is not wanting the other person to feel disappointed or angry because of my refusal. What I care about even more is being afraid that the relationship will break because of the refusal.
You seem to care a lot about other people’s feelings, and also care a lot about your relationship with her, right?
Yes. This seems to have become a kind of psychological burden. I’m always caring about other people’s feelings and ignoring my own needs and feelings.
You feel that in relationships, you need to compromise a lot, and you often ignore your own feelings and needs?
Yes. I feel that the relationship and harmony are more important than my personal feelings. This belief makes me keep compromising, and I’ve even gotten used to this pattern.
Is this way of doing things your everyday pattern? Do you feel this pattern has an impact on you?
Yes. In almost every situation, I do this. I’m always hoping to maintain a harmonious relationship by meeting the other person’s needs.

Being able to notice your own feelings while also respecting other people’s feelings is a balance worth developing. We’re just about out of time for today. Next time, we can continue talking about this.
Okay, thank you for your help today.
You’re welcome.
I’ll think carefully about the issues we talked about today. I look forward to continuing next time.
Was today’s discussion helpful for you?
Yes, it was helpful. It made me start reflecting on my own behavior patterns.
I’m glad to hear you’ve had this kind of reflection. Could you please help fill out the feedback form?
Okay, thank you. I’ll fill it out.
Then shall we meet next week at the same time?
Yes. See you next week.
Okay, see you next week.
Goodbye.
Goodbye. I wish you all the best.

Well, to be honest, I was a little angry at first, but I tried not to bring that emotion into the session. I was worried it might affect our communication.

It’s okay. I think we can talk about some of the issues and questions that have come up during counseling.

I completed the homework from last time seriously, and I did have some new discoveries and reflections.

I noticed that in some situations I become especially sensitive, especially when others give criticism or suggestions. That makes it easier for me to get caught up in my own emotions.
Do you feel you’ve been feeling much better yourself? How do your family members feel?

Yes, I feel I’ve improved somewhat, and my emotions aren’t fluctuating as much. My family has noticed it too. They said my mood has been much more stable recently, and communication with them has also been smoother.
I’m really happy to hear about these changes. Now you’re more able to do things starting from your own needs and feelings. This is a very important step. Is there anything else you’d like to share?
Mm, there is one thing. I’m still confused about the communication we had last time because I asked for leave. I feel like I didn’t handle it well.
Thank you for your honesty. This brought you some distress, right?
Yes. After that happened, I thought about it a lot. I feel like maybe we should have clearer rules between us, so that similar misunderstandings might be avoided.
I can understand how you feel. We can discuss together how to set clearer rules to help avoid similar misunderstandings. How does that sound?
Looking back now, I feel that communication made me realize the importance of rules, but at the same time it also taught me how to better express my needs and feelings.
You recognized the importance of rules, and at the same time learned to express your needs and feelings. That’s very important.
That’s true. I feel that communication conflict also helped me understand how to stand by my own position while still maintaining communication and understanding with others.
Yes, expressing your feelings and thoughts is a very important part of this.
Mm, that really would be tiring. This attempt at communicating made me feel a bit more comfortable, and I could express my emotions and position more openly.
I’m glad you’ve found a more suitable way to express yourself. This kind of progress is really worth recognizing.
Yes, I’ll pay attention to that balance. I hope that while expressing myself, I can also maintain balance.
Being able to notice this balance is important. It will have a positive impact on you and your family.
Yes, I’ll pay attention to that balance. I hope that while expressing myself, I can also maintain balance.
You’re in a very good state right now. I had originally wanted to teach you some ways to express yourself in conversations, but it feels like you already have a very good grasp of it at this point.
Thank you for your understanding. Actually, I’ve been working hard to learn how to communicate and express myself better. This is an important area of growth for me.
Mm-hmm, I understand. This is one of our goals. The progress you’ve made in this process is truly reassuring and encouraging to see.
Yes, I also feel that I’m gradually coming out of it. This process makes me feel fulfilled and hopeful.

If you want to do this in relationships with friends and colleagues, you can try slowly. I believe that with time, you’ll get better and better. This is a process. You can set goals first, and then take it step by step in a grounded way. I understand the effort you’re making.
I understand. Now I’ll take it step by step and not rush for quick results. I believe that as long as I keep at it, I’ll make better progress.
At this stage, it’s normal to allow yourself to be like this. Just like a battery needs charging, we also need time to recover.
Yes, I’ve been through quite a lot during this period, and I also feel I need to rest and adjust properly.
We can take it in two steps. On the one hand, first rest and recharge; on the other hand, learn some new methods during the recovery process. That will be more effective.
That’s a good suggestion. I’ll try to relax myself, and while recharging, also learn some new methods to adjust my state.
Mm, when it comes to friends, the situation can be a bit more complicated. These boundaries are different from intimate relationships, and we need to find a balance that fits.
That’s true. I’ve noticed that in different relationships, different ways of responding and handling things are needed, and I need to find a suitable balance.
Haha, you’ve become a trash can. Mm...
Sometimes I also feel like I’m a “trash can.” My friends always tell me all kinds of problems, and sometimes that makes me feel pressure and burdened too.

I hear you saying that friends often confide in you, and because of that you feel pressure and burdened. Could you say more specifically how you usually handle it when friends come to you with their problems?
That’s true. It makes me feel that I’m valuable, but I also need to learn to set boundaries and protect my emotions from being too affected by negativity.

Considering that you also feel pressure when helping friends, learning to set boundaries and protect your emotions is really very important. You can give yourself some time to rest and see how, in situations like this, you balance this kind of relationship with your friends.
I think for now I’ll choose to rest and recover, while also continuing to learn to set boundaries and protect myself better.

That sounds like a very good decision. We all need time to recover and keep a good mindset when getting along with friends. The reflection and adjustment you’ve been doing during this time should help your overall state.
I think doing this can not only help me recover, but also prevent too much negative emotion from building up, and help me keep a better mindset when getting along with friends.

It’s really important that you can see the balance point in a relationship between two people. Your judgment about this relationship may also lead to a healthier and more sustainable friendship. Adjusting slowly while protecting yourself will make the relationship between you and your friend better.
Yes, I’ll try to find that balance point and make my relationship with my friends healthier and more sustainable.
We’re about at time. Today’s session covered a lot. Next time, we can continue exploring your feelings and changes during this period.
Okay, please go ahead.

Okay, I’ll carry it out.

Okay, Selina. I’ve filled it out. Today I’d like to talk about some difficulties I’ve been having in the dorm lately.
Mm-hmm. What would you like to talk about today?

It’s like this. I have a roommate. At first we got along pretty well, but now she’s become really strange. She ignores everything and leaves early and comes back late every day. I don’t know how to get along with her.
It sounds like this change has been really troubling for you. What does it look like specifically?
Mm, sometimes, like when I’m reading, she suddenly talks in a strange tone, and it makes me feel really uncomfortable.
When she talks in a strange tone while you’re reading, what do you feel?
I feel really irritated, like I’m being disturbed, and I can’t focus on reading.
It seems like it has a big impact on your concentration. Are there any other feelings?
Yes, and sometimes it makes me really angry, but I don’t want to have a direct conflict with her. I’m afraid it would affect the atmosphere in the dorm.

It makes sense that you don’t want to affect the atmosphere in the dorm. That must feel really conflicted. Is there any particular reason you feel it wouldn’t be appropriate to directly express your dissatisfaction?

I don’t want to make it a big deal. After all, we still have to live in the same dorm for a long time. I feel that “hurting” others is not good, because it makes relationships worse, and I don’t like that kind of tense atmosphere.
What is your bottom line?
I hope to have a harmonious living environment, without having to face this kind of awkward and unpleasant situation every day.
You hope that when others get along with you, they can feel comfortable and respected. Is that right?
Yes, I hope everyone can get along peacefully and respect each other’s space and feelings.
What kind of answer are you hoping to get from me?
I hope to find a way for us to get along normally, and not be as awkward and tense as we are now.
Will you be separated in the future?
Yes, we’ll still live together for a while, but after that there may be a chance to separate.
Do you mean there may be a chance to adjust the living arrangements in the future?
Right. Maybe when we’re seniors, we’ll each find a new place to live, and then we can separate.
Mm-hmm. About how long from now?
About half a year, I guess. But during this time I still have to live with her.
Then how do you plan to get along with her during this time?
I want to avoid conflict as much as possible, but I also want to find a way of getting along that isn’t so awkward.
What would a normal relationship look like?
A normal relationship should be that everyone can talk happily and help each other, instead of being awkward and distant like now.
Mm, I understand. Everyone’s definition of a normal relationship may be different. Could you talk more specifically about what the ideal relationship looks like in your mind?
I hope there can be a more open and interactive relationship, instead of almost no communication like now.
It sounds like you have a strong desire to improve the relationship between you. I can offer some suggestions here, or we can continue exploring solutions together. How does that feel to you?
I hope you can ask some questions to help me understand this issue better and find a way to solve it.
Have you had any experience with counseling before?
No, this is my first time coming for counseling.

Okay, thank you very much for choosing to come here. Counseling is a process of exploring yourself. I’ll accompany you as we look for answers together, but the specific decisions and answers will need to rely on your own thinking and insights.
I understand. I’ll try to think for myself and find the answers.
Good. Thank you for telling me your feedback about the issue.
You’re welcome. I feel like this conversation has given me some insight.
I’m glad to hear you say that. So is there anything else you’d like to discuss? If you feel today can end here, we can also continue next time.
I think we’re about out of time today, but I still have a lot of questions, and I hope we can keep talking next time.
Okay, thank you very much for your participation. Becoming the person you hope to be is a long-term process. You’re welcome to continue exploring your concerns next time.
I hope I can become more confident and better able to handle interpersonal relationship issues.
Then what do you hope to get from counseling?
I hope to learn some concrete methods to improve my relationship with my roommate, as well as my overall ability to handle interpersonal relationships.
What made you decide to explore your inner self?

Because I think interpersonal relationships are very important. If I don’t handle them well, it will affect my studies and my life. I hope I can become more mature and better at handling these complicated relationships.
So what kinds of help do you feel you can get from this program?
I think you can help me understand myself better, and how to get along with others more effectively. That’s very important to me.
What is your understanding of it? Could you say a bit more, so we can know different people’s expectations?
I think counseling can provide a safe space where I can speak freely, and receive professional guidance and suggestions to help me solve problems.
Do you feel there are any aspects of our communication that are especially important to you, or that need special attention?

Yes. I hope that through counseling I can improve my ability to think, and have insight like they do. In our communication, there hasn’t been any “passive-aggressive” tone, and I’m very grateful for your professionalism and patience.
Thank you very much for your understanding and cooperation. Counseling requires effort from both sides. We can set a suitable time together to make sure it’s as effective as possible.
Okay, I’ll keep that in mind. Thank you very much for your time today.
Okay, goodbye.
Good evening. I feel okay, I guess, but my emotions keep going up and down. Maybe it’s because of some family factors.
Mm-hmm, go ahead.

Recently I’ve had some conflicts with my husband. He used to always be there with me, but because his father and stepmother suddenly came, I’ve been under a lot of pressure. Now he seems like he doesn’t know how to balance things either.
That does sound really hard to handle. I remember you said before that he would go back to be with you.
Yes, that was what we had agreed on. But now he has to take care of his father and stepmother, so sometimes he just can’t take care of me too.
He decided to take care of his father and stepmother, is that right?
Yes. He feels it’s his responsibility, and I can understand that. It’s just that sometimes I feel neglected.

I can sense that this is really hard for you to accept. You said you put a lot of thought and effort into getting him to come back and live with you, and now with this new change, it really is very upsetting.
Exactly. I spent so much effort asking him to come back and live with me, and now suddenly there’s this new change. I really feel like I can’t quite accept it.
I understand. You put a lot of energy into having him come back, and now these things have suddenly happened. It really would be hard to adjust to. Can you talk more about how you’re feeling?
Maybe it’s because they feel they’re getting older and need someone to take care of them. But I still find it really hard to accept. For all these years, they never contacted us.
You don’t understand it either.
Right. I completely can’t understand it. After all, they didn’t take any responsibility for so many years, and now they suddenly show up. It really makes me feel helpless.
You feel like they don’t seem to have considered your feelings, right?
Yes. It’s like they haven’t considered what impact this would have on our lives, like children who only care about their own needs.
I can sense your helplessness and disappointment. This is a very hard reality to accept.
I also know I have to face it, but my emotions are still unstable. I often feel like I have no way out.

Mm. Hearing this, I feel a bit of sadness. When you say you don’t want your child to inherit the illness, in fact you’re also saying that you yourself, Xiao Zhu, are living a very hard, even painful life.
Yes. I really don’t want my future child to go through the pain I’m experiencing now. Depression and anxiety are truly very hard to bear.
I can imagine how much these experiences have affected your life. It really hurts to hear.
Mm. I don’t want myself to be in so much pain either, but sometimes my emotions are really hard to control.

The internet seemed to have a bit of a problem just now, and my message didn’t go through. Sorry about that. What I was going to send was: because it feels uncontrollable, it feels even more difficult.
Yes. That uncontrollable feeling makes it even more hopeless. Sometimes I really don’t know what to do.
That feeling really is very hard. Can you say more about the despair and helplessness you’re feeling?
I have been keeping records, but I found that my emotional ups and downs are just too frequent, and writing them down makes me feel even more helpless.
Frequent emotional ups and downs really can make that sense of helplessness harder to manage. In the process of recording them, have you noticed any emotions that are especially hard to cope with?
Yes. Lately I’ve also always wanted to sleep. I feel like in dreams I don’t have to face the difficulties in real life.
It sounds like sleeping may have become a way to escape reality. Does this way of coping make you feel a little better?
My mom also feels really sorry for me, but she doesn’t have many ways to help me either. She can only watch me struggle.
Your mom feeling sorry for you and your own struggle not only cause you pain, but also make her feel helpless and distressed. At the same time, what is your relationship with her like?
Yeah. When my mom sees me like this, she gets very anxious, and then I feel guilty too. After all, my illness also makes her worry a lot.
My sense is that’s part of it. And of course, I think there’s another layer too—it must be a mother’s heartache for her daughter.
Mm. My mom always hopes I can live well, but she also knows what my situation is like right now.
It sounds like your mother really cares about you.
Sometimes I feel like I’m really useless. I always need other people to take care of me, but I can’t bring them any benefit.
It feels like you’re carrying a lot?
Some people might think I’m very selfish, putting my emotions onto my family, but they don’t know my pain.
It sounds like those comments really make things hard for you.
Maybe some relatives and neighbors. They don’t know much about my family’s situation, but they like to butt in.
Your relatives and neighbors don’t understand your situation, yet they still make judgments. That really is hard to deal with.
Yes, close family members can understand my pain, but outsiders often look at me with prejudice.
It sounds like you’re saying those judgments are still there, but you don’t care about them anymore now, is that right?
Yes. I’m trying not to pay attention to that gossip now, and focusing on my own recovery.
From caring about it in the past to slowly wanting not to pay attention to it now, what happened in between?
Maybe I’ve slowly realized that no matter what other people say, I still have to manage my own life. No one can solve my problems for me.
It sounds like you’ve had a lot of new realizations.
So I just feel that no matter what other people say, the key is still to find ways to help myself get better.

From a practical point of view, other people can’t really interfere in our own lives, so we really don’t need to pay attention to them. But this truly takes a lot of courage. People are social beings, and China in particular is a society with very close relational ties. That’s why I say this way of thinking is very brave.
Thank you for affirming that. I’m still trying to learn to be a little braver.
You’ve been learning and growing all along, and that’s really not easy. Could you say more about how you’ve managed to do that?
Sometimes I feel that if I hadn’t gotten sick, I might be living better.
Mm, I can understand how you feel. It’s very normal to have thoughts like that.
But now I can only accept reality, try to live each day well, and stop letting myself sink into regret.
It sounds like you’re very strong. Being able to find a positive mindset in a difficult situation is really not easy.
We’re not in touch that much, because he has to take care of his father and stepmother, so he’s pretty busy too.
Mm, it seems like he really is very busy. So have the two of you made some adjustments in how you communicate?
Sometimes I do want to contact him, but I’m afraid of bothering him, so I feel really conflicted.
That conflicted feeling is very normal. You hope for more support, but you also don’t want to add to his burden.
I don’t know how it will turn out in the end, but I hope we can get through this difficult time together.
I understand your hope—that you can face this together with your partner. I hope the two of you can find ways to support each other.
