I feel a bit sad, but maybe I have to try doing this. Maybe I should accept him as he is now, instead of always expecting him to be like the person in my memory.
You’re right. Accepting the current situation is a very important step. We can take it slowly and see what can help you cope with this change better.
I’ll try to do that. Accepting the current facts and letting go of those previous expectations—though it’s hard, it might also be good for me.

I’m glad you’re willing to try. In this process, if you can still keep some expectations for the future, that may be more helpful for you. At the same time, allowing yourself to experience the feeling of disappointment is also an important part of it.
I’ll try to accept my own expectations, and I’ll also work on letting them slowly fade. I hope I can get through this feeling.

We don’t need to rush. What matters most right now is helping you feel a little better. You’ve always cared a lot about other people’s feelings, and that shows how thoughtful you are. But remember, that doesn’t mean you did anything wrong. You’re not wrong. We covered a lot today—shall we continue next week?
Thank you, teacher. What you said is very true. I’ll think it over carefully. See you next week.
Okay. If you need anything, feel free to let me know anytime.
Okay, I’ll contact you anytime. Thank you for understanding.
Okay, we’ll meet on Wednesday. I hope everything goes well for you.
Hello, teacher. I feel like my situation is getting worse and worse.
Good evening. How have you been feeling lately?
Not very good. Sleep problems have been bothering me all along, and I feel especially anxious.
It sounds like things really haven’t been easy for you lately.
Yes. These past few days have been a lot better, but it’s still really hard to actually fall asleep.
I understand. That kind of situation can be really troubling. Have you noticed any changes in your mental state?
Yes. Every night it feels like my mind just won’t stop. The more I try to sleep, the more I can’t.
That state can really wear you out. Is there anything in particular that’s making you worry like this?
Not entirely. I just came back to school recently, and it’s been hard to adjust my routine. It’s like there’s always this thought controlling me, afraid that I won’t be able to sleep.
Coming back to school may bring a lot of new challenges and pressure for you, and those can all affect your sleep. Are there any other reasons you feel might also be affecting you?
In the past few years, my life has changed a lot—from school to work and then back to school—so my rhythm of life has become unstable.
I can understand that. An unstable life rhythm really can bring a lot of stress and anxiety, and make it hard to adapt. What do you feel has been the biggest impact of these changes on you?
Yes, I’ve tried a lot of methods, but the effects are all temporary. I always feel like I can’t solve the problem completely.
Mm, I understand. It must feel really frustrating to have tried so many methods without any of them truly working. Could you share what kinds of methods you’ve tried?
I went to see a doctor, but the doctor just prescribed me some sleeping pills. The effect wasn’t obvious, and I don’t really want to rely on medication.
I can understand your concern. Relying on medication long-term really isn’t the best solution. What exactly did the doctor suggest at the time?
The doctor said my situation might be related to anxiety and suggested I do some relaxation training and counseling, but the results still haven’t been obvious.

It sounds like you really have tried many different approaches. Relaxation training and counseling may take some time to show results. Have you felt that any relaxation methods helped you a little, or were there parts of counseling that felt not very effective?
I know medication can help me fall asleep, but I’m worried that relying on medication long-term will have side effects.
Your concern is very reasonable. It’s normal to worry about the side effects of medication. We can explore in more depth whether there are other ways to help with sleep. How does that sound?
Also, recently I’ve realized that falling asleep is actually only part of the problem. More of it is the psychological pressure and anxiety.
Mm-hmm. Why do you feel unable to quiet down?

I always feel like there are a lot of things spinning around in my mind. Little things that happen during the day make me think about them over and over, and on top of that, the dorm environment makes me feel a bit pressured.
Does the dorm environment have a big impact on you? Can you tell me more about it?
I’ve tried listening to music and meditation recordings, but the effect is limited. Sometimes they actually make me more awake.
Mm, that kind of method really doesn’t necessarily work for everyone. Have you tried any other relaxation methods?
Sometimes I can empty my mind, but most of the time my thoughts are all tangled up, and no matter what I do, I can’t calm down.
It’s hard for your thoughts to stop, especially at night, right?

Maybe I’m afraid of missing something. I always feel that after lights-out at night, there are still a lot of things I should do but haven’t done yet, and what my roommates say also makes me feel uneasy.

It sounds like you have a lot of worries about the time after lights-out at night—not only about unfinished things, but also that what your roommates say makes you uneasy. What do you feel these worries mainly come from?
Yes. I don’t like other people telling me what to do with my life, but I’m also afraid that if I don’t do things well, it will affect others.
What kind of feeling is that?
An extreme sense of conflict. On one hand, I long for my own space and rhythm; on the other hand, I feel anxious and guilty.
I’m wondering whether your current life is reflecting this state.
Mm, yes. I’m always struggling back and forth in this contradiction and entanglement, and I feel physically and mentally exhausted.
Mm-hmm. These things aren’t clear yet. There’s still room to explore and to look forward to. Would you agree?
I hope I can find a way to balance things, so that I can have my own space without affecting others.
What makes you say that?
Because I feel that if I can find this balance point, I might feel much more relaxed, and my sleep problems might gradually improve too.
I understand. You hope to find a more harmonious way of living—one that meets your own needs while not making you worry too much about other people’s feelings, right?
Yes. Sometimes I feel like everything I do every day is very mechanical, and I can’t see much meaning in it, so I feel a bit lost.
In this kind of daily life, discovering some elements that feel special and enjoyable to you might bring a different experience. Have you noticed any moments that make you especially happy?
You’re right. I really can try to find some joy and value of my own in these everyday things.
Yes, finding these unique elements may make life feel richer for you. Could you talk about what things you’re especially interested in?
Mm, I’ll try to look for those elements and try to make life feel more meaningful.
I’m very glad to hear you say that. I wonder if you’ve thought about what specific actions could help you better experience this joy and value.
Yes. Overthinking and overanalyzing make my life exhausting, and I don’t have that kind of simple happiness.
It sounds like your thinking really has brought you a heavy burden. Maybe we can explore some ways together to reduce this exhaustion.
I hope so. I long to get out of this fog and find light in life.
Your wish is very important, and it also shows that you have a strong motivation to change. We can explore together and see what methods are most effective for you.
I’ll work on exploring and look for answers that suit me, even if there will be confusion and setbacks along the way.
That’s a very interesting way to explore, so you can give it a try.
Okay. I’ll follow your suggestions and go experience and explore new ways.

I believe you have your own thoughts about your current life situation. These explorations of yours will also affect your actual emotions and life. I’d like to first understand what you care about and what you’re thinking about, and then find inspiration for helping you solve the problem. Actually, counseling is also a process of exploring yourself and understanding yourself. I hope to understand you better and then help you.
Thank you for your understanding and support. I’ll think carefully and try to find a path that suits me.
It’s okay. Everyone’s way of thinking has its own characteristics, and there’s no good or bad.
Mm, I’ll try to accept my own way of thinking and slowly figure out its strengths and weaknesses.
It sounds like you already have some direction. I believe this process will be helpful for you. So when would you like to schedule an appointment? Evenings are more convenient for me.
Sure. Then let’s do Saturday evening. That time is more convenient for me.
Sure. Would Saturday evening at seven be okay?
Yes, seven works well.
Okay, seven is great. I’ve scheduled the appointment for you.
Okay, thank you. I’ll be on time.
You’re welcome. See you Saturday.
See you Saturday. Bye-bye.
Goodbye, and I hope you have a good day!
Hello, teacher.
Hi, Xintian.
Actually, I’ve been having some issues recently in how I get along with my boyfriend, and I wanted to talk to you about them.
Mm-hmm. What happened specifically?

One day last week, he said he was going out to eat with friends, and I acted unhappy. He suddenly got really angry and said that every time, I act unhappy, and it puts pressure on him. I realized this might have to do with my mom being controlling toward me since I was little.
It sounds like this has been really troubling for you.
Yeah. I tried hard not to show it, but he still noticed.
From what you’ve described, it seems like you’ve made a lot of effort to regulate your emotions.
I think so too. I could definitely keep working on regulating my emotions better, but sometimes I can’t control myself.
Mm, that does feel really hard. When something like this happens, how do you usually regulate your emotions on your own?
I’ll go running or listen to music, but sometimes those methods don’t fully calm me down.
I understand. Sometimes we need to try different ways before we find the most effective way to relax.
Sometimes I write in my journal and write out my emotions. It feels a bit better.
Journaling is a very good way to help sort through emotions and thoughts.
I think so too, but I always feel like it’s not thorough enough.
That’s understandable. Maybe you’re still looking for deeper reasons and solutions.
Yeah. I really care about him, and I hope my relationship with him can get better.
It’s clear that you value this relationship, and that’s very important.
He actually loves me a lot too. I also know this issue is mainly with me, and I hope I can make changes.
Your attitude of self-reflection is very valuable. That’s the first step toward change.
I want to solve it at the root. I don’t want to keep making him uncomfortable because of these small things.

Mm, yes. When it comes to facing mistakes, we talked about this last time too. 1. After making a mistake, after he blames you, practice the behavioral response based on the new understanding, and see what the results are afterward. 2. Think through three questions. One is: my emotions feel uncomfortable because of this, so how can I release them? The second is: why does his arrogant way of speaking create such strong negative emotions in me? The third is: what could I have done at that moment that would be a behavior coming from inner strength? From this role, do you have any new understanding?
I’ve thought seriously about these questions. I think the key is still in how I manage my emotions and understand things.
Mm, I can see that you’re making positive changes.
Thank you. I’ll keep working on it.
Mm. I notice that your wording is very professional.
Haha, I’m also constantly learning and reflecting. I hope I can become stronger inside.
Mm. When you feel your emotions are especially intense, what kind of state do you think would be ideal in that situation?
The ideal state would be that I can understand his needs, and calmly accept inside that he’s going out with friends.
If he still criticizes you the way he always has, what would your ideal state be after being criticized?
The ideal state would be that even if I’m criticized, I can calmly reflect on my own issues, instead of rushing to defend myself or getting emotional.
I understand what you mean. We can become strong inside, even when we’ve made a mistake.
Yes, I also hope to become that kind of person.
When being criticized by someone close to you, what would the ideal way of responding look like?
To keep facing it calmly, accept the correction, and think about how to improve, rather than falling into an excessive emotional reaction.
You feel this is the ideal state, right?
Yes, I think this is a mature and rational way to respond.

I think that if we make a mistake and are blamed by others, feeling sorry is normal. After all, it is our responsibility. An appropriate apology is also important. In a way, the emotional reaction that comes after making a mistake may help us make fewer mistakes.
Mm, I understand.
It’s just that the degree of this emotion needs to stay within an appropriate range. Do you think your emotional reaction is in the right amount, or is it a bit too much or too little?
I think my emotions are a bit excessive, to the point that I can’t handle this situation completely calmly.
Mm. Then what would be a better emotional state for our ideal state? Making a mistake, and then being criticized by someone close to you.
The ideal state would be to maintain an appropriate amount of shame and apology, and learn from it, rather than falling into excessive self-blame.
Mm. This observation is quite important.
Yes, I’ll slowly adjust myself.
An appropriate amount of negative emotion can indeed help remind you, but the key is not to let yourself fall into excessive self-blame.
Yes, an appropriate amount of negative emotion can indeed remind me to avoid making the same mistake again.
Feeling ashamed after making a mistake is normal. In this situation, do you feel your negative emotions are in the right amount, or are they a bit excessive?
I think they may be a bit over the limit. I’ll work on adjusting them, so my emotions can be more moderate.
Mm, I understand. You care a lot about feedback from people close to you, and that is exactly part of your motivation to adjust yourself.
Yes, I care a lot about his opinions and feelings.

I think caring about other people’s attitudes toward you is also very normal, especially between spouses. But if you care too much, it may have negative effects. So finding an appropriate balance is very important. You can try exploring your own feelings and see what degree is suitable for you.
Yes, I’ll pay more attention to my emotions and my reactions to him, and find a balance.

I understand your thoughts. In a marital relationship, it’s very common to care about the other person’s attitude when being criticized. What’s important is that you find a level of caring about the other person that fits you. This is something you’ll need to sort through and think about yourself, to find that balance. Maybe you can spend some time thinking about this, and we can continue discussing it next time.
Okay, I’ll think carefully about this.

Also, continue with the two assignments we mentioned before. Pay attention to changes and shifts in the situation, and bring those changes back to yourself. We can’t change others, but we can change ourselves, if needed.
Got it. I’ll keep doing that.
Then our goals and tasks for this time are clear. Next, please fill out the questionnaire.
Okay.
Thank you very much for your trust, Xintian. I’m also looking forward to our meeting next Monday at 8 p.m.
Hello.
What would you like me to call you?
You can call me Xiao Li.
Mm, I didn’t see you last week.
Yes, I really couldn’t come last week. My child had a fever, and I needed to stay home to take care of her, so I had to cancel.
That’s okay. Next time, try to attend on time if possible. If you book in advance, there will be a reminder. How have these past two weeks been?
These past two weeks feel pretty much the same, I guess. I’ve been trying hard to adjust my state, but it doesn’t seem to be having much effect.
How has your mood been?
My mood is still very unstable. Sometimes I feel like I’m about to fall apart, and I get angry at my child very easily. Afterward I feel really guilty.
I can see that you’re troubled by your mood swings and by how you react to your child. Have you tried anything to ease these feelings?
Mm, yes. I’ve been going back and forth about whether to get a gym membership, but I still haven’t made up my mind.
What are you worried about?
No, maybe I didn’t explain it clearly. I mean, I feel like the gym is kind of a “sacrifice” for me. I keep thinking about it, but I’m also afraid I won’t be able to stick with it.
It sounds like you have some mixed feelings about the gym.
Actually, every time I get stuck like this, it’s like I keep putting my hopes and reality on an “altar,” making myself endure disappointment and helplessness.
I understand. You feel very helpless.
So I’m even more prone to mood swings.
That sounds really hard. How does it gradually pass?

I try to talk to myself and tell myself that my child is innocent and shouldn’t become the outlet for my emotions. But it’s really hard to do. I often only realize afterward that I did something wrong.
That’s understandable. It takes a lot of self-awareness and self-control.
Mm, when I talk about women’s pain, I mainly mean the depression and anxiety I’ve experienced, and the helplessness that comes from carrying the heavy responsibilities of family and parenting.
What changes do you feel are happening now?
What’s different now is that I can notice my emotions earlier, but I still lack effective ways to regulate them.
Especially with which emotions, like anger?
Yes, especially anger. Whether it’s anger at myself or at my child, I feel like I have nowhere to release these emotions.
These emotions and pressures are affecting you a lot, right?
Yes. It feels like there’s a huge stone pressing on my heart, and even breathing feels a little difficult.
It sounds like you’re really under a lot of pressure, especially when you feel vulnerable.
Yes. I feel like my vulnerability sometimes makes things worse.
When you feel angry, how do you deal with those emotions?
Basically, I don’t. I feel like no one can understand me, and no one is willing to listen to me complain.
What you hoped for wasn’t given to you, and instead you were hurt. That’s very painful.
Yes, that gap makes me suffer even more. Sometimes I really feel so hopeless.
When do these feelings become stronger?
When I feel especially helpless, or when things are beyond my control, that impulse becomes very strong.
It feels like in certain situations, your emotions become very hard to control.
Yes. I feel like I could explode at any moment and do something that can’t be undone.
That sounds really difficult. Are you worried about what kind of impact these emotions might have on you or on the people around you?
Actually, I’m very worried too, especially about my child. I’m afraid I might hurt her.
Are you worried about what kind of impact these emotions might have on your child?
Sometimes I have the urge to hurt myself. I feel like that might make things a little better, but I haven’t actually acted on it.
If you’re living in an unhealthy environment, it really can make positive change more challenging.
Yes. Sometimes I really feel like I can’t get out of this pit.
It sounds like your situation right now is really painful.
Mm, I guess sort of, but it’s still very hard to keep going. Every time before I go out, I have to struggle with myself for a long time.
I can sense that you’re working hard to fight against your own struggle, and that’s not an easy process.
Yes. I really hope there could be someone who understands me and can make room for my emotions.
You hope there can be someone who understands you and makes room for you. That’s a very natural need.
To me, making room for me means being understood and accepted, not being blamed and denied.
Being understood and accepted is very important to you, and I’d also really like to understand how these wounds are affecting you now.
Some wounds are still bleeding, but some seem to be starting to scab over. I hope that one day they can heal completely.
The wounds you’re talking about sound very painful. Having a supportive environment would definitely help.
Yes, but very few people can give me that feeling.
Mm, I can feel how much you long for support. What kinds of support feel most important to you?
I understand, but life right now doesn’t seem to have that kind of cooperation and support yet.
Your current situation really does sound very difficult.
Yes. I feel very isolated and helpless at home. Everyone seems to only care about themselves.
It sounds like you feel somewhat lonely and helpless at home.
Only my son. He always loves me unconditionally and needs me.
Your son sounds very special to you. Can you say more about what kind of support he gives you?
He throws himself into my arms and tells me he loves me. His love is the purest.
It sounds like you feel you’re being treated as a tool, rather than as an independent person with feelings.
Yes. I often feel like I’m just a tool being used, not truly a person with emotions and needs.
Is there anything that can make you feel a little better, or help you temporarily get away from this feeling?
Sometimes, yes. I’ve tried to find inner peace through meditation or being in nature.
What are those moments like for you?
The good part is that I can truly quiet down, not be troubled by anything, and focus on feeling the beauty of the present moment.
Do you have a new way of looking at effort?
Yes. I’m beginning to understand that sometimes effort isn’t only for the result, but also for the growth and learning in the process.
You gain more strength from the growth in this process, right?
Yes. When I can connect with that strength, I feel like I’m capable of facing any difficulty.
I’m curious about the kind of relationship you mentioned. What kind of relationship is it?
I mean the relationship with myself and with the world. It’s no longer just about completing tasks, but about finding inner peace.
Then what do you mean by “that’s all”? It sounds like there’s a sense of letting go?
Yes, letting go. Learning to accept my own imperfections and no longer being so attached to outside judgments.
It feels like your connection with your body has become closer, right?
Yes. This is part of what I’ve been trying recently—through some body-based practices, helping myself accept myself more.
This course feels very different from how you used to feel at the gym, right?
Yes. This class focuses more on the connection between mind and body, while the gym is more about physical exercise.
What effects do you feel this change has had on you?
The course is in a group, but there is one coach who makes me feel especially warm.
I see.
His attitude is always very accepting, and it makes me feel very safe.
You can feel that.
Yes. That feeling of being understood and accepted suddenly made my burden feel much lighter.
Not everyone is able to feel that kind of feeling.
Yes. I feel very lucky to have met someone like that.
Is that what you need?
Mm, I think so. Right now I really need this kind of support and acceptance.
This support and acceptance are really important to you. From it, you feel warmth and safety.
Yes. Sometimes these small details make me feel that I still have hope.
You mentioned that these small details make you feel hopeful. Could you say more about what those details are?
Yes, I’m still trying to find that—how to find a healthy outlet.
It sounds like you really want to find a healthy way to express your emotions. That’s very positive.
No. I always feel like I don’t know how to express these inner confusions.
It really does take a lot of courage to express your inner confusion. Would you be willing to share some of these confusions with me?
Mainly, I don’t have friends I really trust, and my family relationships are always not smooth. I feel like I don’t have anyone I can rely on.
It sounds like you feel disappointed in your relationships, and also very lonely. That must be really hard for you.
Yes. I’ve been thinking about what exactly I can do, but I still have no idea.
Finding what you truly want is a process. Maybe we can explore it together and see which areas might interest you.
Yes. Through these conversations and attempts, I’ve noticed a lot of details I hadn’t paid attention to before, and I’m slowly understanding some of my own needs.
Like you said, becoming more positive.
Yes. I hope this positive attitude can help me get out of this difficult situation.
This is really a good start. Keep going with it, and I believe it will have a good effect.
Okay. I’ll try to give myself more patience and time.

Good. If this approach feels comfortable for you now, please continue doing it. Our counseling time is almost up today. I remember you mentioned before that there are some things that are hard to say to a counselor, and one goal we set was to try to express yourself authentically. I wonder if this goal is still important to you?
I think this goal is still very important to me. Like today, sometimes saying it out loud really does make me feel lighter.
I’m glad to hear that. Through expressing ourselves authentically, we usually feel more relieved. Did what we talked about today feel easy for you to express?
Yes. We talked quite a lot today. I feel like I’m slowly able to trust and express more.

Expression really does need to be built on a foundation of trust. If there are some things you can’t say for now, that’s okay. It means you may still need some time and preparation. We can keep working on it together, slowly.
Yes, I can really understand that.
How does it feel to talk with me about these things?
I feel like I can be understood and listened to, and I feel much more comfortable inside.
I’m very willing to listen to you share, and seeing your changes, I’m also really happy for you.
Thank you for your acceptance and understanding. This is really important to me.
Mm, and thank you for being willing to trust me.
I’m very grateful to you, and I hope we can continue discussing these issues next time.

I’m also looking forward to our next meeting. About the extreme thoughts you mentioned before when you feel emotionally overwhelmed, we can gradually talk more about them and find better ways to cope.
So far it hasn’t happened, but I’m also worried about what I should do if I really lose control.
It sounds like you feel very worried and powerless about this issue, is that right?
Yes. This impulse has been there for a long time, but I don’t know why I’m like this either.
I understand. Could you tell me more about this impulse?
No. I try my best to control it, but it really feels awful.
Hearing you say that you’re trying hard to control it, that must take a lot of your energy.
Yes. He is one of the biggest sources of motivation in my life, and I don’t want him to get hurt.
Your love and care for your son are very important to you, right?
I will. If I really lose control, I’ll seek professional help.
Very good. Seeking help is a very important safety measure. If you feel you need more support, you can tell me anytime.
I understand. I also don’t want to bring harm to myself or others. I’ll control myself as much as I can.
It sounds like you once trusted others, but it seems the result wasn’t very good.
Yes. I once trusted some people, but I didn’t get the help I expected. Instead, I was hurt.
I understand how you feel. I hope I can help you, and at the same time, I also hope you can maintain self-control and keep yourself safe. Do you feel you can do that?
I’ll do my best to make sure I don’t do anything extreme. I don’t want you to worry about me.
Thank you for understanding. I also truly hope I can help you.
Thank you for your concern. I’ll do my best to protect myself.
Okay. If you need more help, please tell me anytime. I can provide some resources and contact information so that when you need it, you can get help in time. Would that be okay?
Okay, thank you. I’ll save these contact numbers in case I need them.

National Life Crisis Intervention Hotline: 400-1619-995 (24 hours); China Psychological Crisis and Suicide Intervention Center hotline: 010-6271-5275. Remember to use these resources when you need them. They can be a great help.
I’ve written them down. Thank you very much.
You can save this.
Okay. I’ll save it and check it whenever I need to.
Okay, then would the same time work for our next session?
Yes. I’ll book in advance and make sure I attend on time.
That’s good. We’ll see each other next week.
Okay. I’ll make the appointment before I get off work today.
Okay, see you next week. I wish you all the best!
Good afternoon, Xiaodai.
Good afternoon. I’m glad to see you again.
Yes, it’s been a while.
How have you been lately?
Pretty lost, I guess. I keep feeling like I’m standing still, and I feel really anxious inside.
It sounds like you’ve been struggling a bit.
It’s mainly that I hate myself. This feeling of being jealous when other people become better really hurts.
I understand. That must feel really painful. Would you like us to start by talking about the issues with studying?
Let’s talk about studying first. It’s been keeping me up at night.
Okay. Can you say more specifically what about it is keeping you up at night?
I want to be at least in the top five in my class, but this time I didn’t get there at all.
How does it compare with before?
Actually, I have improved, but it’s far from enough. I’m still not satisfied.
I see. Do you feel that this improvement, and the parts that still feel lacking, affect your mood?
Yes. I’ve noticed I’m less and less willing to interact with people who are better than me or work harder than me. I always feel like they’re constantly reminding me of my own shortcomings.
Mm, it sounds like you have improved, but you hope you can do even better, is that right?
Yes. There’s always a voice inside me saying, “You can still do better.”
How did you achieve this improvement?
By imitating other people’s study methods and increasing my study time, but I always feel distracted.
Everyone’s way is different. You can look at what methods you’ve used before that worked for you.
Before, when I occasionally settled down to study, I would feel very efficient. But now the pressure is high, and it’s hard to find that state.
Can you tell me in more detail about the difficulties you’re facing right now?
Maybe it’s because I care too much about what others think, and I’m afraid others will surpass me.
What kind of impact do you think caring about what others think has on you?
Yes, every time I feel like my efforts aren’t enough. I always feel like other people are better than me.
Can you talk about the pressure you feel and the results it brings?
There have been a few times, but that was more luck. My mindset is very unstable.
When your mindset is unstable, how do you cope with it?
Yes, every time my grades aren’t ideal, I keep blaming myself and questioning my ability.
It sounds like you have very high expectations for yourself, and that this also brings you a lot of pressure. Is that right?
Yes, but I always feel it’s not good enough. I always feel it’s far from enough.
I understand how you feel. You want your grades to be better.
Yes. To raise my scores, I need to perform well on every exam, but this pressure makes it impossible for me to concentrate.
It sounds like you have very high expectations for yourself, and that can make you feel a lot of pressure.
A huge amount. Sometimes I don’t even dare to face exams, and I worry so much I can’t sleep.
I can sense the anxiety and pressure you feel around exams. Before an exam, what do you usually do to ease these feelings?
Nervous, anxious, afraid of failing. It’s really hard to calm down.
This nervousness and anxiety are understandable, especially when you really hope to perform well.
Yeah. But I always feel like everything is my fault, that I’m the one who didn’t do well enough.
Hearing you say that, I feel you have very high demands of yourself, and it seems like you haven’t left yourself space to rest and adjust. What makes you feel that time is so urgent?
Yes, my busy life makes it impossible for me to focus on reviewing. I always feel like there isn’t enough time.

Not being ignored is very important to you. I hear you saying this isn’t just a simple need, but is tied to your recognition of your own value. How might you better meet this need in your daily life?
Right. I don’t need a lot, but I hope the people I care about can notice my existence.
Mm-hmm, I understand. If you think back, when was the earliest time in your life that you felt this feeling of being ignored?
Mm, that question is a little hard to answer. I need to think about it.
That’s okay. Then how about we talk about a recent experience?
The most recent time was a few days ago. I sent a message to a friend, but she never replied. I knew she had time, because we used to chat often.
Okay, I understand. That was your friend.
Yes, we’re still very good friends.
That makes sense. What made you feel that she had time?
She posted an update on social media, and it didn’t look like she was very busy.
I see. From your description, your relationship with her is very close. Can you tell me what your relationship is like?
Our relationship has always been good, but sometimes there are small conflicts.
I understand.
She probably doesn’t realize how much not replying to my message affects me.
How important is this friend to you? If you were to rate it from 0 to 10, what score would you give her?
Probably around 6 or 7. She’s one of my few close friends.
Okay. Can you tell me what 6 or 7 means to you?
A 6 or 7 means she’s an important friend, but not the most important one. We have a lot of topics and experiences in common.
Got it. Have you tried telling her your expectations about replying to messages promptly?
Maybe she doesn’t really know. I haven’t clearly told them.
Perhaps this could be an opportunity to open up communication. You could consider sharing with her your feelings and needs around this.
Yes, sometimes I also feel like I’m the one asking for too much.
Mm-hmm. I think maybe everyone has different expectations about replies to messages, and they may not care about this as much.
Right, they really don’t care about these details as much as I do.

Earlier we talked about how these friends are people you’ve been in frequent contact with recently, and that you hope to maintain friendly relationships with them. I’m a little curious—what are some things about them that you especially appreciate?
There are many things about them that are worth learning from, like being optimistic, cheerful, and their ability to handle things.
Mm-hmm, I see. It sounds like you’re very happy when you spend time together.
Yes, a lot of the time we have a great time chatting together.
From your description, I feel that your relationship seems pretty good.
I hope so, but sometimes I’m not too sure.
That’s understandable. When you feel anxious, perhaps you can try doing something else to shift your attention and help yourself relax a bit more.
Mm, maybe I can try this method, and not put all my attention on waiting for a reply anymore.
Mm-hmm, that sounds like a good thing to try. I hope you can gain some new experiences and feelings from it. We’ll continue discussing this next time.
Hello, my last name is Zhang. Today I’d like to talk with you about my child’s situation and my worries about him.
I’m glad you’re willing to come and talk about this, Mr. Zhang. Could you first briefly tell me about your child’s situation, and what you’re worried about?
I’m his father. Yes, I hope I can learn more about ways to help him.
I understand.

My child is quite introverted and not good at communicating. Last year, right before his final exams in the third year of high school, he suddenly called home and said he felt awful, that he was having thoughts of ending his life and couldn’t sleep. We quickly took him to a brain hospital for an examination.
I may need a bit more information before I can know how to better help him. Could you briefly tell me about his situation, starting from when the depression first appeared?

Around the second year of middle school, he started showing some behaviors that didn’t seem quite normal. For example, when throwing out trash, he was always afraid he had thrown away something useful, and would repeatedly go back to look for it. After leaving the house, he would often turn back to check the door locks. Also, he walks a bit on his toes, and he may have been laughed at by classmates because of that, so he became very self-conscious and always felt like people were talking about him.
Mm-hmm. So from the second year of middle school until now, what has his medication treatment and counseling been like?

Actually, before the third year of high school, we just thought he was somewhat sensitive and self-conscious. We didn’t realize he had depression, so there wasn’t any specific treatment. It wasn’t until he called and said he was having thoughts of ending his life that we started taking it seriously.
What was the diagnosis at that time?

The doctor diagnosed him with moderate depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder. Later, he was prescribed four medications: sertraline dispersible tablets, alprazolam tablets, quetiapine tablets, and Annao pills.
I see. How long has it been since that diagnosis?
A little over half a year.
Mm. Was he taking the medication regularly before? After stopping the medication, did he go back for any follow-up visits?

We’ve always had him take the medication on time and in the prescribed amount. Every month, we take him for a follow-up visit, in case there are any adverse reactions to the medication or it needs to be adjusted.

I understand. You’ve been very responsible, and that’s very important. Actually, quite a few studies show that combining medication treatment with counseling tends to work better. For treating depression, medication can help control symptoms, but counseling can help him understand and work through his emotions at a deeper level. If you’re considering counseling for him, it really would be a good addition.

I understand. So we’ve also been especially careful about making sure he takes his medication on time. But we still feel it’s necessary for him to get some psychological counseling, not just rely on medication.

Also, if he has mentioned thoughts of ending his life before, or shown similar signs, we really do need to pay close attention. When inner pain has no way to be released, it can build up into more serious problems. Helping him find some effective ways to regulate his emotions would also be very helpful in reducing his suffering.
Yes, we’re indeed very worried about his mental state, and we don’t know how to help him regulate his emotions.

Mm-hmm, I understand your worry. If we can help him better understand and manage his emotions, and support him through these difficult periods, the thoughts of ending his life may gradually weaken or disappear.
Yes, we hope he can get out of this emotional difficulty as soon as possible.
I think his current situation still needs fairly close attention.
Thank you for your advice. What can we do to help him regulate his emotions?
There are quite a few ways to regulate emotions. I recommend that you read a book called Dialectical Behavior Therapy.
Okay, I’ll look for this book and read it. I hope it will help.
For emotion regulation, one way is to shift attention, using the senses—sight, hearing, smell, and taste—to help soothe the painful feelings inside.
Okay, I’ll try some ways to shift his attention.

Second, when he feels intense inner pain, for example late at night, mindfulness meditation can help him not be overwhelmed by his emotions. If you need more help later, you can book another counseling session.
That’s okay. I’ll contact you again. Thank you for your help.
Second, when he feels intense inner pain, for example late at night, mindfulness meditation can help him not be overwhelmed by his emotions.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll learn about mindfulness meditation and try it.
Before he fully recovers, combining medication treatment and counseling, along with his own regulation and the family’s companionship, will help him as much as possible.
I understand. Thank you.
Okay, thank you for your understanding. If you feel it’s needed, you can schedule the next counseling session anytime.
I think we may still need more advice and help. I’ll book another session.
Also, if you’re willing, you can help me fill out a feedback questionnaire. We can just agree on a time.
Okay, I’ll fill out the questionnaire. Can we schedule it for 10 a.m. tomorrow?
Okay, please wait a moment. We can schedule it for 10 a.m. tomorrow. Are you available at that time? If you have another time, you can also let me know.

Lately I’ve been feeling a bit tired, and emotionally pretty weighed down. I’m still keeping up this friendly and well-behaved front, so it looks like everything is okay, but actually I don’t feel good inside. Sometimes I feel like it might be easier to be dead.
It sounds like your emotions and mental state have been really hard on you lately. Have you thought about talking with anyone about these feelings?
Creatively, things are going fairly smoothly. I’m trying to release these suppressed emotions through art. Even though it’s very difficult sometimes, creating itself really does give me some comfort.
It’s really good that making art can give you some comfort. Can you talk a bit more about how you feel when you’re creating?
Yes. I often think my current state is like a flower in the dust. It looks insignificant, but it’s still trying hard to bloom.
That’s a beautiful metaphor, and a powerful one too. Can you say more about what makes you feel like a flower in the dust?

Yes. I feel like I’m always struggling against the heavy pressure of life, like trying to bloom while struggling in the dust. On the surface everything looks normal, but inside I’m actually in a lot of pain.
It sounds like, in facing the heavy pressure of life, you’re feeling a lot of pain and struggle. Can you talk more about these feelings?

Yes. I’ve found that when I’m maintaining this surface-level normalness and friendliness, I’m actually a bit like some of those “too nice” people I know. On the surface, everything looks calm, but they’re actually carrying a lot of inner pain on their own.
These “too nice” people you mentioned sound like they’re enduring a lot of inner pain. Do you feel you’ve had similar experiences too? Could you say more about that?

Yes. I feel like these feelings gradually built up over time. Maybe because I’ve been constantly dealing with the pressures of life and relationships, I’ve started to feel more and more emotionally suppressed inside.
The feeling you described, of suppressing what’s inside, sounds very heavy for you.
Maybe. I feel like I need some way to face my inner distress and pressure in a grounded way. But in reality, I’m always suppressing myself, not letting others see my vulnerability.
You long for a way to face stress openly and steadily, but you also don’t want others to see your vulnerability.
Yes. I feel like maintaining surface calm and trying hard to deal with the heavy pressure of life will gradually wear away my spirit and my passion for artistic creation.
You’re worried that, in the process of dealing with life’s pressures, your creative inspiration and passion will be damaged.

Yes, that’s exactly it. Although I believe art needs to draw inspiration from life, the heavy pressure of real life makes me feel that sometimes I can no longer find that pure creative passion, and I’m also worried that I’ll lose myself under the pressure of life.
You hope to draw inspiration from life, but the heavy pressure of life makes it hard for you to keep your creative passion, and you’re also worried about losing yourself.

The more whole personality I want might be one that can still keep inner calm and creative freedom when facing pressure, without being troubled by the small matters of life and interpersonal relationships.
You hope that while facing pressure, you can keep inner calm and creative freedom, without being troubled by the small matters of life.
Mm, yes.
I’m also curious how you’re able to separate these feelings while facing life’s challenges. How did this shift happen?

I don’t know exactly how the change happened, but I think maybe because I went through a lot of pain and struggle, I gradually learned to look for a point of balance within the suppression. I’m not willing to sacrifice everything for the sake of a whole personality, but I hope I can find a way to keep peace of mind without suppressing myself.
It sounds like, through these experiences, you’ve found some balance and learned how to deal with your emotional needs.
Yes. Although the process was very painful, it really did teach me a lot, and it also helped me understand more clearly what I need inside.
I can understand that. In this process, what did you sacrifice your own needs for?
I used to always want to sacrifice my own feelings and needs so my family and friends wouldn’t worry. I was always afraid that if I showed my vulnerability and pain, they would feel really bad.
I can imagine that this persistence and stubbornness have carried you to where you are now, but at the same time they’ve also come with some challenges.
Yes. My stubbornness has supported me until now, but I also know I’ve been pushing too hard all along, and I haven’t truly taken care of my own emotional needs.
Listening to you talk about these experiences, it feels like you now have a new understanding of your past persistence and sacrifice?

I now feel that who I was back then was actually avoiding the fear and unease inside, using self-sacrifice to look for a kind of false comfort. Looking back now, I realize that although this way worked in the short term, in the long run it caused me more harm.
I see. This realization may bring some new insight for your life going forward.
No, I don’t want this stinging pain anymore. My past experiences have helped me understand that only finding myself within balance is what’s truly important.

Mm. When you say that, what do you feel? I’m wondering if maybe it’s precisely because these emotions were so deeply painful that your pursuit of something beautiful became strong enough to reach the point of self-sacrifice.

When I say that, I feel a sense of release. Yes, perhaps it’s exactly because of these deep pains that I became so persistent in pursuing beauty. But now, I hope to find a healthier way to realize myself, rather than through self-sacrifice.

It’s a process, I think. If you hadn’t had that pain before, you wouldn’t be who you are now. After experiencing those limits, the grounded clarity and sense of spaciousness you feel allow you to look at yourself and the world again. Your art has become deeper and more meaningful because of this, hasn’t it? Mm, human emotions.

Yes. This process really has helped me grow a lot. Although it was painful, it was also a kind of tempering, and it made me understand more how to cherish everything I have now. Human emotions really are a complex and wonderful experience.

I’m very glad to witness this part of your inner journey, and I also feel very inspired. During the pandemic, I also experienced some feelings around facing real-life limitations, and they were more tolerant and expansive than I had imagined. I’m curious about your exploration of the emotions of ordinary life.

I’m now starting to learn to find small moments of happiness and satisfaction in daily life, and to feel the meaning of existence in tiny, insignificant details. This exploration has given me a new understanding of relationships and life, and has helped me see more beauty.
Mm, this process symbolizes a kind of growth, I think. Responsibility and taking things on really can bring pressure.

Yes. Sometimes responsibility and taking things on do feel really heavy, but I hope I can find a way within balance to no longer suppress myself, and instead truly face these responsibilities and what I have to carry.
Have you ever imagined what the balance you hope to reach would look like?
Sometimes I imagine a world without pressure, where everyone can express themselves honestly and doesn’t have to suppress their true feelings inside just to maintain surface-level peace.
Are you saying you’re worried you won’t be able to express your true feelings?
Yes. Besides love, there are many complex emotions, like fear, anxiety, and loneliness. Sometimes these feelings are very vague, but they’re also rooted very truly in my heart.
These emotions have a deep impact on you. Do they affect other parts of your life?
Yes. This suppression sometimes affects my work and studies, makes it hard for me to concentrate, and also makes my emotions very unstable.
Are you afraid of showing your vulnerable side?
I’m afraid that if I show my vulnerable side, the people around me will feel disappointed or upset. I don’t want to become a burden to them, so I always keep these feelings pressed down inside.
I understand. This experience has left a deep shadow on you. Becoming aware of this is the first step toward healing. Shall we continue exploring this next week?
Good evening. I feel really tired today.
I can understand how you feel. It sounds like you really went through a lot today.
Mm, thank you. I understand. It’s just that lately the pressure has really felt a bit heavy.
Yes, feeling under a lot of pressure is really not easy, especially when we have a lot of tasks to get done.
I actually really don’t like unexpected situations. When things don’t go according to plan, I get really irritated.
I understand. You prefer doing things according to plan, because that helps you feel more in control. What happened today that made you so tired?

After my night shift today, I went home thinking I could get a good sleep and then do things according to plan. But for some reasons, I wasn’t able to finish the tasks I had arranged on time, and it felt like the whole day was ruined.
That sounds really hard. Not being able to follow the plan can definitely feel very frustrating. How are you feeling now?
Yes, my mood is really bad. I have no motivation at all.
I can sense your frustration and helplessness. It really is upsetting to run into a situation like this. You need some time to rest properly and adjust a bit, right?
Yes. I feel like if someone were there to remind me and support me, it might be a little better.
Mm-hmm, go ahead.
Sometimes I feel like I can’t cope with these emotions, and I can only silently bear them by myself.
It sounds like these emotions make you feel very alone and helpless, right?
Yes, I remember.
Can you say a little more about these emotions and feelings? For example, how do they affect you?
Yes, but not much. I always feel dissatisfied with how I arrange my own time.
Mm, I understand. This kind of situation is very common. You mentioned the reading plan we talked about last time. Did it help you distract yourself or ease things a bit in some way?
About two or three pages, and after that I just couldn’t get myself to keep going anymore.
I see. Sometimes it’s really hard to find lasting motivation. Maybe we can explore together some other ways that might be helpful for you?
Mainly my mood is bad. I feel like I can’t do the things I planned well, and inside I’m always very anxious.
I can sense your unease and anxiety. Is it because you’ve been thinking about the exam that you feel this way?
Yes. I’m worried I won’t meet my expectations, so I’m constantly in a state of anxiety.
I understand your worries. This kind of pressure is really not easy. What do you think has kept you from reviewing?
That’s true. Sometimes after work I’m really tired. Even though I want to study, I often don’t have enough energy.
Mm, I can understand. After work, it really can be exhausting. Sometimes we clearly really want to do something, but we just don’t have enough energy.
And once I feel like I can’t do something well, my whole emotional state collapses, and then everything afterward becomes really hard to carry on with.

When your emotions collapse, it really is hard to do anything else. What you’re feeling right now must be very painful. Do you feel it’s mainly the lack of energy that has a bigger impact, or the anxiety inside?
Maybe both. Lack of energy and the anxiety inside both make up a big part of it.
I see. The pressure from both sides is really heavy. Can you tell me what your daily schedule looks like? We can look together to see if there’s any room for adjustment.

I get off work at nine in the morning, eat and rest for a while until about eleven, and then the plan is to sleep until five in the afternoon. After that, I’m supposed to do yoga, study and review, and take care of some small things.
Mm-hmm, and then?
But often because I’m in a bad mood or physically tired, I can’t do any of it well, and then I just don’t want to move at all.
I see. That must feel very frustrating. What do you think is the main reason for your bad mood or fatigue?
Yes, that’s part of the work, but I feel a lot of pressure, and it’s hard to balance.
It sounds like these tasks are putting a lot of pressure on you. Can you say more specifically what makes it feel so stressful?
Because I’m very worried that I’m not doing well enough, and I’m afraid of making any mistakes. That makes me feel extremely pressured.
I can understand how unpleasant this worry and fear must be for you. Has anything specific happened recently that made this feeling especially strong?
Sometimes I feel that no matter how hard I try, I can never meet the overly strict standards I have in my mind.

I hear that you have very high expectations for yourself, and maybe that makes you feel even more pressured. Is there any method or support that could help you relax a little and reduce this pressure?
No. I always feel that I should complete these tasks on my own. This is my responsibility.
It sounds like these tasks are especially important to you.
Yes. She’s always bringing up tasks in my ear, and she always expects me to complete them perfectly, which puts a huge amount of pressure on me.
These expectations make you feel a lot of pressure?
In a way, yes. She just keeps putting more pressure on me.
You feel that she has a lot of expectations of you, right?
Yes, because I feel like things are already hard enough for me. I hope to get some understanding and support, not even more pressure.
It feels like you really hope to get her understanding and support, and to reduce the pressure a little.
No. I’m afraid she’ll think I’m making excuses and not trying hard.
These things make you feel very exhausted, right?
Yes, I really feel exhausted, physically and mentally.
Mm-hmm. What do you think is the main thing?
Mainly that I have too high expectations for myself. No matter when, I’m constantly adding more burden onto myself.
What do you usually do after you get home at night?
I do some housework, like laundry and tidying the room, and then I try to study and review, but often it doesn’t go the way I want.
Mm-hmm, lots of little scattered things.
Yes. There aren’t that many things, but each one has to be done well.
So about how much time do these things take up?
Yes, but even so, I still feel a lot of pressure at home.
For things like laundry that you mentioned, if you don’t delay or drag things out, how long do you estimate they would take altogether?
About an hour or so, if things go smoothly.
Mm-hmm.
But sometimes I just can’t finish smoothly, and I keep dragging it out.
It seems like this is an area where we could think of ways to improve. What do you think?
I also hope I can find a way to improve it. I don’t want to always be stuck in this kind of negative mood.
I understand. Can you say a little more about how you feel? For example, in the evening, what usually delays you?
Yes. I hope I can finish everything before eight in the evening, and then have some time of my own to rest a bit.
Mm-hmm, I understand that your goal is to finish everything before eight in the evening. I think that goal is very clear. Where do you think it might be easiest to start improving?
Okay, I’m willing to try.
Then maybe we can set a short-term goal, for example trying it for one week first, until this Friday. How does that sound?
Okay, I’m willing to try.
Great. What do you think would make it easier to do?
Maybe if I break the tasks down more carefully and only finish one part each hour, it might be a bit easier.
Do you think changing it to before eight-thirty would make the schedule a bit more reasonable?
Maybe eight-thirty would be more reasonable. Having a little more time could reduce some pressure.
That sounds like a good idea. We can try putting it into practice for one day tomorrow first and see how it goes.
Okay, I’m willing to give it a try.
Okay, then tomorrow evening we can talk again about how you felt after trying it.
Okay. I hope I can get a little better.
Do you think if you rest well now, you might feel more energetic tomorrow to face the tasks?
I think so. If I rest a little better, tomorrow I may have more energy to face them.
Okay. I hope you can get a good rest tonight.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll go back and try them out.
Mm, okay. I look forward to continuing to discuss your progress with you tomorrow.
Good morning, counselor.
What would you like to talk about today?

Lately I’ve been feeling really lost, and I don’t know what to do. I feel like my head is a tangled mess, with no plans or goals at all. I don’t really think there’s anything wrong with me, but people around me all say I’m avoiding reality and responsibility, and that leaves me really confused.
Can you describe what exactly they say when they say you’re avoiding reality and responsibility?

Okay. My girlfriend criticized me, saying I don’t face and solve real-life problems. For example, on Monday, I was playing games, and she asked me to take care of some things at home, but I just dealt with them half-heartedly. Later she blamed me and said I’m always like this, avoiding responsibility.
How did you feel inside when your girlfriend criticized you?
Honestly, when I saw how angry she was, I did realize the problems and responsibilities were there, but I just felt that facing and solving them was too much trouble. I’d rather avoid them.
It sounds like you do hope you can face these problems, but the process feels very stressful for you, right?
Yes, it really isn’t easy. Sometimes I also wonder if I can truly face these real-life problems, but every time I think about all that trouble, I want to back away.
That’s a very normal feeling. Facing real-life problems can indeed be difficult. If we explored some coping strategies together, do you think that might help?

Mm, maybe. My girlfriend’s strategy is to keep reminding me, sometimes even saying things very harshly. She hopes I can take responsibility on my own initiative, instead of waiting until problems come up and then trying to cover them up.
I understand. Do these reminders happen often in your interactions?

Her actions haven’t caused any bad consequences, but she reminds me and pushes me every day. And I feel that this constant reminding actually makes me feel a lot of pressure, and that’s when my anger flares up.
I see. When do you feel this pressure started?
Maybe after we made the relationship official. She started noticing that I wasn’t willing to take responsibility, and then she began reminding me constantly.
What effect has this pressure had on your relationship?

A lot of negative effects, I guess. Every time she reminds me, I get really irritated, and then we argue and give each other the silent treatment. Our relationship is getting more and more tense. Every time we talk about the future, I feel very unsure.
It sounds like these reminders make her tense too, and that may further affect your relationship?
Yes. Once she gets tense, she becomes emotional and pushes me even more. This cycle makes our relationship really bad.
Mm-hmm. Has this anger been showing up more often or less often recently?
More often recently, because we’ve been talking about getting married lately, and these issues make her even more tense.
Why do you think the topic of marriage makes her so tense?
Yeah, sometimes I really feel this kind of life is too exhausting, and I do have thoughts of breaking up, but I also can’t bear to let her go.
It sounds like you feel very conflicted in this relationship—there’s pressure, and at the same time you feel you can’t leave her.
Yes. Once I get angry, she gets very scared, and then both of us are unhappy.
Has this happened many times? Would you be willing to talk about it?
No, this has already happened several times.
How do you understand these reactions of hers?
The first time it happened, I felt she was caring about me and reminding me. But after it happened more and more, it instead made me feel blamed and pressured.
The way she expresses herself makes you feel pressured, right? Do you think she may also be holding some things in when she expresses her feelings?
Maybe she thinks communication is the only way, but the way she does it is sometimes very intense, and that makes me feel scared and resistant.
It sounds like you don’t want her to suppress things, but you also don’t want her to express them emotionally, or explode. So what kind of expression would you hope for?
I hope she can be a bit gentler and give me some time and space, instead of constantly pushing me.
When she’s with you, is she often able to express her emotions calmly?
Not very often. More of the time she’s pretty emotional, especially when it comes to relationship issues.
Is not expressing herself something you like?
Not really. I hope we can communicate, but not the kind of communication that feels suffocating.
What proportion of your relationship would you say is made up of that relatively gentle kind of communication?
Very little, probably less than 20%.
Mm, I can see that you really do hope there can be more gentle ways of communicating.
I understand. Basically, when she expresses her emotions steadily, we’re usually in a better place.
Can you tell me how often that happens?
Probably only once or twice a month. Most of the time it’s emotional communication.
You just mentioned understanding how she usually holds things in, and that she truly expresses her emotions. After understanding it this way, does the fear become a little smaller?
A little bit, but it doesn’t completely ease. I still feel this kind of communication is really uncomfortable.
You said it’s okay to have a bit of emotion sometimes, but “shouting in anger” is not okay. Does shouting in anger happen often in your relationship?
More than once. It’s become a lot more frequent in the past few months.
When she’s emotionally unstable, does it make you feel afraid?
Yes. Every time after we argue, I feel extremely scared, and I even wonder whether we should break up.
How long does that fear usually last?
A few days, I guess. I only feel a little more at ease once we make up.
And the thoughts of breaking up? How long do those feelings last?
About the same length of time. Sometimes it’s just a momentary impulse.
Communication seems to play a very important role here?
Yes, we need better ways to communicate.
What do you think could help avoid this kind of situation next time?
Maybe we can work together to find better ways to communicate, instead of having intense arguments.
Do you think that in communication, sometimes you may express yourself rather strongly too?
Possibly, because sometimes I also get impatient, and both of our emotions aren’t very good.
Mm-hmm, I understand. This way of communicating may escalate the tension. We can explore some more constructive ways of communicating together.
I hope so. We can try to change this way of communicating.
Has her relationship with her family also had an impact on her?
Yes. Her family also has very high demands and expectations of her, and that may put a lot of pressure on her.
Understanding her relationship with her family is indeed important. What specific effects does that have on the two of you?
I hope so, but the things that happened in the past are still hard to completely forget.
Yes, past experiences are hard to completely erase, but with understanding, it may be possible to ease some of the emotional burden.
Yes, I get very angry and don’t want to listen to what she says at all. I just want to end the argument quickly.
When you’re angry, you feel unwilling to listen to her anymore, and you’d rather end the argument quickly, is that right?
I hope she can understand my feelings, stop pushing me, and give me some support and encouragement.
You hope she can understand and support you more, and that would feel better for you. In your conflicts, do you think she takes timing into consideration?
Sometimes she thinks her arrangements are right, but in reality she often overlooks some practical circumstances, and that also leads to a lot of conflict.
You feel that her overlooking things and thinking her arrangements are right has caused a lot of problems, right?
Yes. I hope she can admit her mistakes and not always make excuses.
It seems like you really hope she can face and acknowledge her own mistakes.
Yes. Some past relationships also eventually broke down because of this kind of issue, so I especially care about this.
So this kind of attitude is very sensitive for you because it touches on some of your past experiences.
I feel disappointed and helpless. I feel like these problems can never be solved, like there’s a huge hole in life.
Mm, that feeling of disappointment and helplessness is like a gap in life that’s hard to fill, right?
Yes. I really hope we can get along well, but every time these issues come up, I feel exhausted.
It sounds like you’re really putting a lot into this relationship, and these issues truly leave you worn out.
Yes. I really hope we can get along well, but every time these issues come up, I feel exhausted.
Feeling so many difficulties and so much exhaustion, while still hoping to get along well—that persistence is really not easy.
Yes, because I love her, but I also hope she can change and not always be like this.
